item.title: The October inflection point for vibe game development
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: I've written before about how November 2025 was an inflection point for coding agents - the point where Opus 4.5 and GPT-5.1 crossed a tipping point that meant their respective coding agents became reliable daily drivers for software engineers. I think we've reached a new inflection point in October 2026, and this time it's for vibe coding computer games.Claude Opus 5.5 in particular exhibits meaningful improvements in several areas needed to build a compelling game:That last one is particularly important. Models have been able to create something that like a game for quite a while now, as seen in my previous experiments. The challenge has been getting to a game that's actually .Game design is a deep subject area. I won't pretend to be well versed in it - I know enough to have respect for it as a craft. Creating a novel, compelling gameplay loop which challenges players at the right level and provides a satisfying learning curve is a fine art. I didn't think the models could do it.Then I tried telling Claude Opus 5.5 to "Make it a LOT more fun"... and it did.In the past few weeks I've vibe coded (in the classic sense of the term - no looking at the code at all) four games that I've genuinely enjoyed playing.I attended Foo Camp in Berkeley over the weekend and met several people who were having similar experiences. Building games that play well is shockingly easy now. The new challenge is coming up with concepts for games that are novel and delightful and that wouldn't exist without AI assistance.I haven't done an exhaustive study, but my current impression is that GPT-6 Astra isn't there yet. It can absolutely build a game, but its sense of fun doesn't match that of Opus 5.5. I expect OpenAI will get there by the end of the year.Here are the four game projects that have convinced me that the models are now capable of producing fun games with very little guidance. All four are built in HTML and JavaScript and run entirely in the browser.The smallest game I found to be genuinely delightful is Tree Appreciator. I used the regular Claude chat interface for this - it didn't even need Claude Code.I built this on a whim while we were driving along Skyline Boulevard looking at trees. My prompt was:Build a three js game called "Tree appreciator" - it shows you two algorithmically generated trees and the game mechanics is about appreciating the differences between them. Think hard about how to make sure it is both fun and beautiful.I've found that telling models to use three.js works really well. Claude doesn't have its own image generation model but is capable of building full-color 3D models that look and feel excellent.This game required no iteration or follow-up prompting at all - I got the game in a single shot. It gave me back a charming little mobile-friendly spot-the-difference game. You can play that here. Here's the chat transcript that built it.It's pleasingly relaxing. The graphics are fun, and collecting trees that you have completed in a "herbarium" provides a nice, cosy sense of accomplishment.This was a more ambitious project that I again built using regular Claude chat. I started out by building an experimental prototype of an engine for a top-down fantasy RPG:Build a demo game engine three.js which is a top down (but at an angle) RPG - the player gets to move through the world with one or two companions. Create a fantasy village setting that demonstrates walking around outside and then shows how when the player enters a building the wall between the player and the camera goes transparent so the user can see what is happeningAdd some NPCs and plenty of furniture and different types of building some with an upstairs - be creative, make it look greatI was inspired to increase my ambitions:Make it not so flat - the buildings are great but the landscape itself is completely flat at the moment, fix thatAdd basements to two of the buildings with a tunnel system joining them below the villageAdd the start of a rocky mountain on one side of the village containing a cave with a sleeping trollWhen produced a good result, I decided to push it all the way:Now turn this into an actual game - quadruple the size of the playable area, introduce fun game mechanics, add a plot that isn't too cliche, some twists, a magic system, make it really goodWe're back to prompts like "make it really good" here! Asking for a plot that "isn't too cliche" seemed to work too - it's a bit cliché, but still novel enough that I enjoyed following the story.Unlike Tree Appreciator, this took quite a bit of additional playtesting and prompting to get to a finished version. This was mainly due to gameplay problems - things like a character not being in the right place to complete a quest because a different story element had caused them to move to another location.Here's that final game. It has a full story that takes about 15 minutes to play through.There's even an experimental level editor if you want to drop in your own houses, furniture, and landscape features.Once it was all working (and I'd iterated through some gameplay bugs), I played it through from start to finish and found myself emotionally affected by the ending! I'm somewhat embarrassed by this, because in this game - the graphics, the plot, the characters, the music, the dialog - came from the model. My creative input was pretty much just "it's a fantasy village and there's a troll asleep in a cave".I also fed that same initial sequence of prompts through ChatGPT GPT-6 Pro. Here's the transcript and the finished game for comparison. It looks great, but I don't think it plays nearly as well.This is by far my most successful project, which I wrote about last week. It's a Command & Conquer-style Real-Time Strategy game where two robot armies (or four as of Saturday) build units, harvest scrap, and battle over territory.This is also the project that convinced me that Opus 5.5 knows what "fun" is.The first versions were built back in July using Claude Fable 5. It got me to a workable 2D Command & Conquer-style game, but it wasn't great to play.I prompted Opus 5.5 to "Make it a LOT more fun" and then later to "Port this game to three.js" and the game was transformed. There's a blow-by-blow account (prompts included) in my write-up.Today, Battle Drones has 2-4 player multiplayer (via a vibe coded WebSockets relay server), medals, replays, seven maps, a random map generator, and a set of "mutators" that add variants of the rules.It also lets different LLMs play against each other, using a mode where the game advances five seconds and then pauses to give different models time to interpret the new game state and line up their next set of commands. Here's a replay of Claude Haiku 5.5 vs. GPT-6 Luna:I released Battle Drones under the Apache 2.0 License last Tuesday. On Wednesday Gabriel Turpin released Panache (screenshots here), a fork of Battle Drones that reimagined the game for steampunk 1900s Belle Époque France, with new models and music and an animated intro sequence. Open source at work!Pumpkin Farmer, aka Quarter Sun CoveI decided to try building a game that wasn't just a cheap imitation of something that already existed, so I set out to create a game about farming pumpkins, growing giant pumpkins, and handling the rush of the October pumpkin season.I called it "Quarter Sun Cove".I'm still iterating on this project, but it's shaping up quite nicely. It's a cosy farming simulator where you spend the year tending to your giant pumpkin and planting out regular-sized pumpkins for sale in October, then sell pumpkins during pumpkin season and enter your giant pumpkin in the weigh-off.Every character in it is a (vegetarian) animal. The mayor of the town is a pelican. You can be a pelican, skunk, raccoon, possum, beaver, coyote, fox, owl, sea otter, or harbor seal. Those species all later show up (accompanied by their children) to buy pumpkins from you.You can play the latest version here. I'm not convinced by the game mechanics yet - it's actually quite complicated: you have to decide when to plant pumpkins such that they will become ripe at the weekends in October with the most visitors.I told Claude to "surprise and delight the user frequently" and the result is little details and easter eggs. There are mischievous raccoons, an elephant seal that runs the weigh-off, harbor seals that roll their pumpkins back into the ocean, a wandering goat, and superstitions about growing giant pumpkins that come true.This isn't my best game yet - it's not as fun to play as Battle Drones - but it represents the kind of game I want more of: weird, fun, uniquely personal - something that wouldn't have been built in the before-times.If you are offended by AI-generated art, AI-generated music, AI-generated writing, and AI-generated code, I have bad news for you: vibe coded games combine . I respect those opinions, even though I don’t strongly hold them myself.The wider games community already has an aversion to AI-generated assets in games. This has been a growing issue over the past few years as tools like Midjourney have enabled developers to generate assets for their projects. This IGN story covering complaints about slop in Valve's Steam Next Fest is a good recent example.We now have games where - code, assets, dialog, and even the game design itself - can be outsourced to the models. And the results don't suck!Building a computer game used to be one of the most challenging projects in all of software development, combining a diverse range of skills and requiring intense focus and effort over many months or even years. And now here I am spitting out a playable multiplayer RTS by prompting on my phone!I expect that, as we've already seen with programming, this will result in a split. Some players will refuse to have anything to do with games that were built in this way. Others may embrace this as opening up game development to a much wider audience. I lean in that direction!I certainly won't be entering any of my vibe coded games in traditional game jams or competitions - I don't feel like I've earned that right. We'll likely see new avenues emerge for vibe game developers to compare their projects.What happens if someone actually puts the work in?The thing I find both exciting and shameful about this is that I have got interesting results from . The projects I've described here are loosely ordered by how much effort I've put into them. Not a single project represents more than four hours of my work (plus many more hours of Claude Code churning away by itself).Now imagine what could be achieved by anyone who takes this seriously, invests significant creative time, applies better taste in game design, and then playtests and iterates on the result until it's as good as they can make it.I want to see games that wouldn't have existed without these new tools.Building games in this way is . It's the perfect application for vibe coding because it's so low stakes: how much damage can you cause with a bug in a personal vibe coded game project?(OK, you can do some damage... my attempt at audio-based multiplayer gave my wife Natalie a nasty headache!)All of my games so far have been HTML and JavaScript using static hosting (generally GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages). Modern browsers - including mobile browsers - are incredibly capable. Frontier models already know libraries like three.js and Phaser. I'm finding these mobile web games to be indistinguishable from the native experience, at least for the kinds of games I'm trying to build.I suggest starting with a prompt like this:Build a mobile-friendly three.js game where...Switch to Codex or Claude Code once your project passes the proof-of-concept phase.And if the game isn't fun enough, add this:

item.title: How to win at Monopoly
item.author: Minnesotastan
item.content:encoded: With a second monopoly completed, your next task is to improve those properties to three houses each, then all of your properties to four houses each. Six properties with three houses will give you more than half of the houses in the game, and four houses each will give you 75% of the total supply. This will make it nearly impossible for your opponents to improve their own property in a meaningful way. Keep the rulebook nearby once the supply gets low, as you will undoubtedly be questioned on it. At this point, you will be asked repeatedly to build some friggin’ hotels already so that other people can build houses. Don’t.At this point, you more or less have the game sewn up. If losing a normal game of monopoly is frustrating, losing to this strategy is excruciating, as a losing opponent essentially has no path to victory, even with lucky rolls. Your goal is to play conservatively, lock up more resources, and let the other players lose by attrition.Most board games are intrinsically competitive, but Monopoly does tend to bring out some of the baser instincts, and as Jason notes, it can also provide uncomfortable reminders of income inequality and business malfeasance in the real world.

item.title: There Might Be Some Life In This World Series Yet
item.author: Ray Ratto
item.content:encoded: This World Series felt like it was in danger of losing its steam, as they all do when one team begins forcefully applying a throw pillow to the face of the other. The Milwaukee Brewers had kept the Tampa Bay Devil (yeah, we said it) Rays at arm's length through each of the first three games, and even though those had been interesting and even occasionally wacky games, they all ended the same way. The specter of a cold winter and uncertain spring loomed larger with each evening's parade of invincible Brewers relievers.Thus, the desperate need for a complete and utter piefight in Game 4, with extra innings, bonfires in both bullpens, a hilarious ending followed by a more hilarious ending to that ending, and, best of all, an additional game of baseball. Game 5 is tonight, and will be played between two teams that now seem just a bit better matched than they had four-and-a-half hours earlier.The basic cadaver of the story is this: Tampa won Game 4 by the score of 4-3, in 12 innings. In so doing, they extended the Series at least another day and put off the moment when everyone who cares about baseball will have to start thinking about the impending lockout. But the autopsy is always about the details, and it is the way in which the Rays went about the business of desperate flailing that breathed new life and interest into what had become a slightly too clinical clash of champions.

item.content:encoded: Four years ago today, I created this newsletter with the half-baked notion that I might try my hand at writing something longer than a tweet.I had no expectations of . If I had, I might have spent more than ninety seconds coming up with the name for this site.I figured I might write a couple of things a week for a little while, grow tired of it, and then move on to the next shiny object.that’s not how shit went down at all Here we are, four years later — and wow, .That is flattering and humbling and … I really didn’t see it coming.FOLKS, YOU ALL FUCKING RULE.I want to thank everyone who signed up to receive the emails — and I especially want to thank all the people who have become commenters here.Really. I reading your comments. I love it when you folks banter with each other. So many of you are clearly wittier and more knowledgeable than I — and I that. It’s nice to be part of something positive — and not, like so much of the internet, toxic and hateful — and I have all of you folks to thank for that. have made this place what it is.Without you, I’d just be shouting into the wind — and that shit gets old .Let me once again take a moment to say thank you to the thousands of people who have posted, commented, private messaged, texted, and phoned to offer condolences. I love you all. I am blessed to be surrounded by an amazing, caring community. I love you all.Thank you for hanging in there with me.And, on that note, let us now have our Daily Claudia.Today, Ms Spouse is going to blow out the birthday candles — first at the Hudson Valley Steakhouse in Yorktown Heights, NY, on February 11, 2022.Have a great Wednesday, everyone. I’ll be back tomorrow, as always, to document the atrocities.Happy fourth fucking birthday to all of us.here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Silver Linings Playbook (2013)
item.author: Minnesotastan
item.content:encoded: I first saw Silver Linings Playbook when it was released back in 2013, but I seem not to have blogged it at the time. I'm doing so now for two reasons, one of which is to save and share the "Girl from the North Country" song by Bob Dylan, which was featured in the movie (some listeners will recognize the second voice in the harmony as that of Johnny Cash). The subtitles are intermittently inaccurate; for lyrics see the link).But I'd also like to recommend the movie, which to be honest is not easy to enjoy at first. Even on a rewatch knowing how much I enjoyed it the first time, it was still difficult for me to tolerate either of the main characters for the first half hour or so of the movie. Bradley Cooper and Jennifer Lawrence portray characters whose behavior varies from annoying to repellant, but by the end of the movie one finds oneself cheering for their success in overcoming their anxieties and obsessions.For those curious about the movie I'll also embed the standard trailer below; the image quality is poor, but it offers a better presentation of the storyline than the musical version at the top.

item.title: Leadership Dispatch: Leading from below
item.author: bounces+qdumm2z8xes7hvg4dzxblh889o44lf4hl36q@ckespa.joshdoody.com
item.content:encoded: This week's Leadership Dispatch is about leading from below. This may be the most difficult kind of leadership—leading when you're not the one in charge. The key is to identify when it's appropriate to be a good team member, helping move things forward, and when it's right to raise your hand and offer suggestions to leadership.This may be the most difficult type of leadership.There will be situations where you are a team on paper but, for whatever reason, you have insight or experience that is equal to or even exceeds that of your team’s leaders.In situations like this, you may find that you frequently disagree with leadership’s direction, decisions, tactics, or other aspects of the team’s work. You may feel a strong urge to express those opinions, but you’ll mostly want to resist that urge.Reserve the times to talk with the leadership team for when you are substantially opposed to their plan because you’re concerned it will cause significant issues down the road. And when you share that sort of feedback with them, be sure to privately correct, publicly praise; that principle applies here as much as anywhere else.The best way you can lead from below is to try to lead in situations where you are concerned about a bad outcome. If you are constantly offering input, nitpicking, and otherwise trying to insert yourself into the leadership process, you will eventually be ignored.​“The Boy Who Cried Wolf” is a cautionary tale here. You don’t want to offer input so frequently that you are ignored the one time it counts.Build up your credibility and use it only when it really matters.

item.title: Chemotherapy
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: Kurzgesagt doesn't usually tell personal stories, but this one is different, and it's full of science anyway. Philipp Dettmer, the founder and head writer of Kurzgesagt, went through chemotherapy treatment for cancer in 2018. A few years later, he is ready to tell the story, narrated by Steve Taylor and illustrated in the neon minimalist Kurzgesagt style. The drug is called Cisplatin. Like most chemotherapy drugs, it is very toxic and does quite bit of damage to a human body. Cancer therapies were developed by calibrating how much was required to kill cancer without killing the patient. That's why chemotherapy is so debilitating, and only worth it at the end when you are deemed cancer-free. Dettmer explains how Cisplatin was developed and how it works in the body. His body, in this case. It's particularly effective against testicular cancer because of the unique role those organs' cells are designed for. There's a lot of violence at the molecular level, with success at the end. And the cancer battle is directly related to why we have Kurzgesagt in the first place. The story is only 12:24; the rest is promotional.

item.title: Breaking Bread
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: The midterms will likely come down to issues that live at the intersection of affordability and corruption. The question is whether the average American can afford to live there. The economic issues at the center of our current campaign go far beyond a single election. The promise of the middle class and the American dream has been broken as our economic bifurcation becomes as dramatic as our political divides. The path to getting a little more and a little more has been replaced by a road less traveled, where middle class Americans find themselves making do with a little less and a little less. “While by some measures, members of the middle class now earn more than those of prior generations, the Brookings Institution recently found that one-third of the American middle class still can’t afford essentials. And for the rest, the high costs of child care, housing, medical care and other necessities make their incomes feel paltry. So they are trimming, reining in the lives they once expected for themselves.” And the cutbacks are needed because of things that are out of people’s control, tariffs, wars, inflation, and medical costs (not to mention the potential threat of A.I. to the job market). What happens to the American dream when people are too stressed out to sleep? Alissa Quart in the (Gift Article): What America Is Living Without. “What’s lost — good bread, regular haircuts, pets, food delivery, babysitters, fancy face creams — isn’t just stuff. It’s ambition. It’s the luxury of living a life without the constant hum of worry. It’s losing the idea of the future you had in the past. It’s nostalgia for a life that you imagined for yourself that will never come to fruition.” Even attempts at distracting the middle class with bread and circuses might not work anymore. Circus tickets are too expensive.Add to the list of destroyed norms the idea that grand jury requests for indictments almost never fail to meet the low bar required. That was before Trump’s corrupted DOJ took over. In the latest failure, a grand jury refused to indict former White House aide Cassidy Hutchinson. Her crime, apparently, was having the nerve to tell the obvious truth about Trump and his enablers on Jan 6. The cowards who didn’t have the guts to stand by her then, sat back and watched her get indicted for showing the courage they wouldn’t (in between, all the Jan 6 criminals were pardoned). It’s all a reminder that this is not a one-man show. It takes a village to raze a government.+ “President Trump’s success in demolishing the traditional wall between the White House and the Justice Department is apparent at the helm of the agency, now led by his former personal lawyer, Todd Blanche. Mr. Trump’s reach can also be seen in the network of U.S. attorneys across the country who are flexing their power to pursue the president’s political agenda.” Here Are the U.S. Attorneys Who Are Carrying Out Trump’s Grievance Agenda.+ “Mr. Witt’s explosive testimony, offered at a hearing in Federal District Court in Washington, was the latest account of just how tight a grip the White House has on decision-making at the F.B.I. and just how willing Mr. Patel has been to take orders from the president to go after people he believes to be enemies.” White House Has Tight Grip Over F.B.I. in Pursuing Trump Targets, Agent Says.The result of the Israeli election could lead to another election. “Israel’s political leaders were poised for weeks of negotiations over the shape of the next government, as initial results on Wednesday showed no clear winner in a tightly fought election that many have described as a make-or-break moment for the country. If neither Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s hard-line alliance nor an opposition bloc led by Gadi Eisenkot win enough seats to form a government, both would need to find support from outside their blocs for backing as prime minister.” Here’s the latest from the NYT (Gift Article): In Tight Israeli Election, Leading Parties Face Tough Path to Power.+ “The voting results are mostly in, and they are less conclusive than everyone hoped, and than either side is willing to admit. (Both sides have said the results show that the public favors them.) Netanyahu’s current coalition can no longer form a government on its own. Neither can the opposition.” (Gift Article): Israeli Election Results Hazy, Try Again.+ “Negotiations to form a coalition will take dizzying twists in the coming weeks; maybe a minority government or a stalemate will be the unsatisfying result. But one thing is certain. Israel’s divisions have never been more profound. Blocs, camps and tribes have never been more irreconcilable.” A bitter night in Israel for all who craved a fresh start.“‘A lot of what we get out of this class is the human experience, and you can’t get that out of AI,’ said Peggy Urdan, a government and neuroscience major from Lexington, Mass. ‘The only way to get anything out of this class is to not use AI.’ At the core of the humanities is, of course, humanity.” (Gift Article): The Brutal Harvard Class That Suddenly Everyone Wants to Take (alt link). “It’s an ungodly amount of reading and no easy A. So why are freshmen lining up to get into Humanities 10?” Either it’s a tiny backlash to AI, or the students really liked watching . “A high-speed passenger train rear-ended another near Toledo, months after a crash involving the same carriers killed dozens and stunned the country.” At Least 68 Killed in Train Crash in Spain. “The accident happened after traffic control operators told a high-speed train to continue its journey when another train was stopped farther along the tracks, Spain’s transportation minister, Óscar Puente, said. He called the operators’ instruction ‘inexplicable.'”+ Give me your tired acts, your poorly behaved, your huddled asses yearning to breathe free from justified prosecution. Flávio Bolsonaro Lands in Miami After Fleeing Brazil. (It’s also troubling that the elected government in Brazil would go after a political opponent so quickly. Who do they think they are, America?)+ “Three brothers convicted of leveraging their wealthy lifestyle to drug and rape dozens of women were each sentenced Tuesday to 30 years in prison after one victim described her attack as an ‘eternity of terror’ and the judge slammed their behavior as shameful, degenerate and monstrous.”+ Under a Different Influence: “In recent years, an average of 30 people a day in the U.S. have been killed in vehicle crashes involving drugs including methamphetamines, cocaine, painkillers and marijuana — meaning at least one driver tested positive for drugs other than alcohol. Yet local, state and federal officials are failing at the most basic levels to confront the carnage.” America Waged War on Drunk Driving. Now, a New Epidemic Is Taking Hold. (Waymos don’t party.)+ “In the summer of 2025, a staffer for Mary Peltola, the Alaska Democrat who was eyeing a run for Senate, received unusual instructions from top campaign aides: Find as many people named Dan Sullivan in Alaska as you can.” (Gift Article): Inside Democrats’ Secret Effort to Stack Alaska’s Ballot. (I once tried to compile an exhaustive list of Dave Pells, mostly because I was hoping to find someone else to read through this hell every morning.)+ “Dolores Huerta, arguably the nation’s most well-known Latina civil rights leader, has died. She was 96.”+ “The Federal Trade Commission has sued the bargain chain Dollar General for what it characterized as ‘long-running deceptive pricing practices’ by charging customers more once they reach the register than the prices that are displayed on shelves and in advertisements.”

item.title: Conspiracies are everywhere thanks to Trump’s ‘voter fraud’ bounty
item.author: 1axbjrc70lq48oxwe4scqeviyd6adgbti3pa6r@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: No one is happy about Tina Peters’ big segment on 60 Minutes this week.The former GOP clerk in a 2021 voting system breach driven by election conspiracy theories was the subject of a segment on the CBS program, which focused on the great lengths Trump went to try to get her out of prison. Peters was charged with state, not federal, crimes, so he had little to do except pressure Gov. Jared Polis (D), who caved and commuted her sentence in May.It should come as no surprise that 60 Minutes — which has been in a complete tailspin since Bari Weiss was put in charge of CBS News — totally botched the segment. Peters and her allies are pissed that it didn’t vindicate her false and deranged claims about voting machines. More importantly, voting rights advocates and election officials are rightly angry that CBS platformed a dangerous conspiracy theorist. All of this makes me wonder: Who was this for?“Hummmm it appears 60 Minutes is trying to cash in on …what did they call me?” Peters , apparently mad they called her an election denier. “Stay tuned while I set the record straight on their heavy editing to distort the truth. Coming up… wait for it! Shame on you from (sic) profiteering off of my incarceration and pain.”“Tina Peters continues to sow distrust in our free and fair elections,” Sen. John Hickenlooper (D-Colo.) chimed in on social media. “She's guilty as sin and a disgrace to Colorado.”Meanwhile, 60 Minutes correspondent Bill Whitaker interviewed Polis, who continued to defend his decision to pardon Peters — even after she’s shown no remorse for her actions and continues to spread dangerous anti-voting conspiracy theories.“I hope that she understands that what she did was wrong,” Polis told Whitaker.

item.title: Across the Horizon Ep. 73: Mary Lattimore
item.author: Flow State
item.content:encoded: On today’s episode of Across the Horizon, Bob Holmes of the band SUSS is joined by harpist and composer Mary Lattimore, one of the curators of Across the Horizon Volume 2. They talk about her contributions to the series as well as those of her guests, Nailah Hunter and Meg Baird. Mary also brought along a playlist of music she’s been listening to the Italian village of Tatti, her new part-time home. The playlist includes Yo La Tengo, Windsor for the Derby, Daniel Ogren, and more.Collected Pieces: 2015-2020 is a great survey of her work, showcasing the way she manipulates the harp sound with pedals to create atmospheres of profundity. , her collaboration with vocalist and composer Julianna Barwick, came out in January. They recorded in a Paris museum, Lattimore using three golden harps from the 18th and 19th century and Barwick using synths and a vocoder. “It was terrifying to hear the cracks when tuning the harps; they’re very delicate instruments,” she tells Bob on the show. “You think about the person who played them last, the person who initially built them…”

item.title: Humpday Hottie: Kaley Cuoco
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: Kaley Cuoco is an American actress and producer best known for her work in television, particularly for playing Penny on the enormously successful sitcom . Born in Camarillo, California, in 1985, Cuoco began acting as a child and appeared in commercials and television programs before landing roles that established her as a recognizable young performer.Her early breakthrough came with the sitcom , where she played Bridget Hennessy. The series gave Cuoco significant exposure and helped establish her as a talented comedic actress. She later joined the cast of during its final season, expanding her television résumé.Her biggest success arrived in 2007 when premiered. Cuoco played Penny, an aspiring actress and waitress who moves into an apartment across the hall from physicists Leonard Hofstadter and Sheldon Cooper. Penny’s personality provided an important contrast to the show’s highly intellectual characters, and Cuoco became one of the central performers in the series. The show ultimately ran for 12 seasons and became one of television’s most successful sitcoms.After , Cuoco demonstrated a different side of her acting abilities in the HBO Max series . She played Cassie Bowden, a flight attendant whose life becomes complicated after she wakes up beside a dead passenger. The series combined comedy, mystery, and drama, earning Cuoco multiple award nominations.Cuoco has also worked extensively as a producer through her company, Yes, Norman Productions. She has continued appearing in film and television while developing projects behind the scenes.With her combination of comedic timing, dramatic range, and production experience, Cuoco has successfully moved beyond the sitcom role that made her famous. Her career has evolved from child performer to sitcom star and ultimately to an established actress and producer with a diverse body of work.

item.title: proxelar
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: proxelar is both a CLI and TUI proxy that inspects and can capture and modify incoming HTTP, HTTPS and WebSocket traffic directly from your terminal.Applications send traffic through proxelar's local proxy and it can extract displays headers, request bodies and individual streaming WebSocket frames. Like similar proxies, this terminal tool can also interactively Intercept pauses in HTTP requests for live editing before forwarding or dropping them with a custom response and captured requests can be replayed / repeated to the server.proxelar has partial support for modern protocols such as HTTP/3, QUIC and Lua hooks can automate request and response changes, including returning mock responses from a reverse proxy. Sessions can be exported as HAR files or curl requests to be repeated or raw HTTP text requests.Developers interested in network traffic analysis or security-focused engineers and researchers who need to test API behaviour by manipulating responses or requests can use proxelar to inspect traffic send from cilent-side applications or devices.

item.title: kernwatch
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: kernwatch is a low-level Linux terminal monitor that focuses specifically on kernel activity and performance tracing.It monitors the internal state of the running system kernel which displays detailed information on CPU scheduling, task memory, interrupts, cgroups and kernel modules inside of the system. eBPF captures allow kernwatch to measure wake delays, syscall durations and request latency with suitable kernel features and permissions.In the 'flame' menu, it has a built-in profiler that allows you to select captures CPU stacks of running programs and compares their traced stacks with the saved baselines. Recording sessions are supported for offline replay of system activity and you can export them to preserve observations and diagnostic findings for later analysis.kernwatch is for those who are performance engineering specialists, Linux administrators, system engineers and even Linux kernel developers that need a single terminal tool that assists with troubleshooting issues on their Linux machine and investigating low-level kernel issues.

item.title: termtastic
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: termtastic is a terminal client for sending messages and inspecting Meshtastic radio networks.It connects to a compatible Meshtastic device over connections such as Bluetooth LE, Wifi, LoRa or serial which it can automatically discover near-by devices on the network. You can reply and send reactions in channel chats and in direct conversations (DMs). All chats and connections made within the Meshtastic network are encrypted at the packet level including DMs that communicate through the network.The node list in the TUI shows each connected node's statistics and telemetry information such as the signal readings, uptime, position, last-heard times and the last hop count. This terminal client allows for sorting and filtering for finding particular devices on the network and you can traceroute a node to show the packet's route through the mesh network. termtastic is for those who are engineers, developers or hobbyists in radio hardware or decentralised mesh networks who want to use a minimal terminal client to exchange messages and examine how neighbouring nodes connect through a mesh network regardless of the connection type.

item.title: spor
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: spor watches your files while you work and saves a snapshot every time something changes, so every past state stays recoverable. Jump back to an earlier point and continue from there in a different direction, without losing the path you came from. Everything is automatic and local.Auto-snapshots every file change into a branching history you move through freely, jumping back and forking off without losing any version. Drive it live from an interactive TUI or with one-shot commands. Local, deduplicated, compressed.spor is for anyone whose work is exploratory rather than planned. Creative coders, designers, writers, data folks. Use it when you try things, back out, and try another direction, and don't want to lose any version you passed through.

item.title: sqlmux
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: sqlmux is a TUI database client with split panes and edit safeguards with a Vim-style SQL editor.The default layout is a 2-split pane with the open databases on the left and the results on the right or in separate tabs and it can connect to PostgreSQL, MySQL, SQLite, SQL Server and Redis connections in a shared tree. It has a read-only mode for dry-runs, which is useful for querying results before running them for real.Additionally, it has auto-suggestions as you type and after executing them, it can suggest tables, columns and functions in the editor where table edits are staged until saving. It has a powerful command palette which displays a view of every quick action you can do to and can run Quick SQL statements from anywhere in the program.This tool is useful to engineers, system administrators, database, backend developers and DevOps engineers who want an all-in-one terminal database client with strong permissions and safeguards built-in with a rich interface to access multiple DBs in the the terminal.

item.title: clavirio
item.author: Curator
item.content:encoded: clavirio is a touch typing tester with tutor guided lessons and timed practice sessions inside of your terminal.It has step-by-step lessons that introduce keys by finger pair and keyboard row. The lesson sequence supports keyboard layouts such as QWERTY, Dvorak and Colemak layouts which you can change at any time. A virtual keyboard below shows the corresponding finger position and the selected keys as you type the text that appears on the screen.Practice typing modes include common words, programming terms, custom text and drills for weak keys. Live feedback displays typing speed, accuracy and errors. clavirio saves session histories and accuracy for individual keys and after each session, a results graph shows speed statistics and the weakest-key option with suggestions for further practice.For technical learners such as developers, technical writers or hobbyists that use the terminal can practice touch typing with visible keyboard movements and track their improvements over time.

item.title: Revised Exit Polls
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: There are three major exit polls in Israel. Two of those three have now revised their estimates to a tie between the two blocs with 51 seats each. The third still has it at 52 for the change bloc and 50 for the Netanyahu bloc. That’s only a single seat difference from the earlier estimates which all had a change lead. But it’s a pretty significant single-seat difference since it gives the two blocs an equal number of seats. It remains mostly symbolic since neither side is anywhere close to 61 seats. But for the narrative, vibes, claims to the legitimacy, it shifts things at least somewhat. – 8:33 p.m.: Likud and the Netanyahu bloc continue to improve over the initial exit polls. Of the three main exit polls, two show a 51-51 tie and the third shows a 52-49 lead for Netanyahu’s bloc. These still leave both blocs far from the minimum of 61 seats to form a government. But as I noted above, it gives Netanyahu more of an argument for a “win.” Interestingly, the exit poll that shows the 52-49 Netanyahu bloc lead shows the “change” bloc losing one of those seats to the Joint List, which in that exit poll gets 12 seats. Likud officials are reportedly telling journalists they’re expecting their bloc total to rise to 55 or 57 votes. Obviously, talk is cheap. You can spin as much as you want. But I don’t have a good feeling about this trajectory.

item.title: Yet Another Weaponization Fail for Trump
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: A D.C. grand jury has refused to vote for an indictment of Cassidy Hutchinson, the one-time first-term Trump aide who became a star witness for the House January 6th subcommittee that investigated the attack. Obviously it’s good that illegitimate attempt failed since Hutchinson is guilty of nothing more than acting honorably. It’s embarrassing for the administration since it’s hard to fail at the grand jury level where the government is literally in charge of everything. But there’s something deeper and more important here: the un-strategic, increasingly impulsive and ultimately self-defeating nature of the Trump legal retribution campaign.

item.title: Have We Confused Having Good Taste With Being Creative?
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: In a world where cultural knowledge has become its own form of social currency, knowing the right designers, listening to the right music, and recognizing the right references can make someone appear just as creative as the people actually producing the work.We’ve reached a point where an entire identity can be built around what someone consumes, collects, wears, and shares. And while developing good taste requires curiosity, knowledge, and an understanding of culture, recognizing something exceptional isn’t necessarily the same as creating something exceptional.This doesn’t mean curation lacks creative value. Some of the most influential figures in fashion, art, and music have shaped culture through their ability to recognize talent, connect ideas, and introduce people to things they otherwise might never have discovered.But there’s a difference between being influenced by something and simply reproducing its appearance. Creativity requires more than understanding what has already been accepted. It often means taking risks, developing an independent perspective, and making something that people might not immediately understand.One of the slides puts it more succinctly:We live in a time where curation can look like creation. A person can build an entire identity out of taste alone — what they wear, what they repost, what they collect, what they reference — and still never actually make anything that moves culture forward.

item.title: An Israel Election Nugget on Prediction Markets
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: As you know, I take a pretty dim view of prediction markets, especially for capturing anything more than conventional wisdom when it comes to election outcomes. There’s also a whole controversy about how much prediction markets are vulnerable to insider trading. But the truth is that insider trading is actually an intentional feature of prediction markets. Perhaps not literal insider trading — as in an officer of a public company placing bets on non-public information — but people trading on non-public information. Indeed, many don’t remember this, but one of the seemingly harebrained ideas to come out of George W. Bush’s first term Pentagon was the idea of creating a terrorism prediction market. I’m not kidding about this. It would have basically been a Kalshi or Polymarket about future terror attacks, with the idea being that you’d get people with knowledge of future of attacks to place wagers, and thus, give U.S. policy planners and counterterrorism officers leads on future attacks.In any case, I note this because again, the real logic of prediction markets is you get the people with the inside dope to place money making bets on future outcomes. You thus use the incentive of winnings to work to pull information out of the realm of secrecy into the open.

But relatively small shifts in the final result versus the initial exit polls could make a big difference.

item.title: The Kingmakers. Maybe.
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Earlier today I discussed how the initial exit polls show an inconclusive result of today’s Israeli election. Roughly 52 seats for the change bloc, 50 for the Netanyahu bloc and perhaps 18 for the two predominantly Arab/Palestinian parties. So what’s the story with those 18 additional seats, which could, in theory, provide either bloc with a comfortable majority?This is a complicated question, but I’ll try to give as simple an overview as I can.There is a big taboo in the Jewish Israeli body politic on governments relying on the votes of the non-Zionist or anti-Zionist/predominantly Arab parties. Depending on how you want to look at it, this is either the ingrained nationalism/racism of Israeli society or the fact that these parties don’t accept the foundational idea of the state. I think the best answer is that there are strong dimensions of both. It’s fair to note that the Arab Druze population of Israel serves in the IDF, is integrated into society and votes overwhelmingly for the various predominantly Zionist parties. Other Zionist parties, especially on the left have, or have had, Arab Knesset members and Arab voters. But the simple reality is that Jewish and Arab/Palestinian voters in Israel vote overwhelmingly for predominantly Jewish and predominantly Arab parties.

item.title: Israel Election Results Spin War Commences
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: As I noted in the previous post, we now have the initial exit polls from today’s election which show the “change” bloc bigger than the Netanyahu bloc but likely only by two or three seats. You have 17 or 18 seats for the two predominantly Arab parties, a historic high, based on historically high turnout today among Israel’s Arab/Palestinian citizens. Voting is only stage one of an Israeli election. Now you have to see who if anyone can form a government. It’s not at all clear that anyone will be able to. But with this mixed result you now begin a public battle over the meaning of the results. The opposition is out quickly with a pretty strong argument. The current government has gone from 68 years to apparently 50. That’s a very big drop and as they put it a massive repudiation. It’s hard to argue with that. On the other hand, the “change” bloc seems to have 52 or 53 seats. Again, according to the initial exit polls. So they “won” in some sense but judged in these terms it’s not like they crushed the Netanyahu bloc.

item.title: Israeli Exit Polls: No Clear Victor
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Israel polls are now closed and we have the first initial exit polls. Note that those exit polls are not necessarily correct, just like in the US. They project the anti-Netanyahu bloc ahead but with Likud (Netanyahu’s party) the largest single party. (That can matter for who gets first shot at forming a government; but the decision is solely that of the President.) Critically, neither side has a clear path to a 61 seat majority. The specifics are 53 seats for the change bloc; 50 seats for the Netanyahu bloc; 17 seats for the two predominantly Arab parties (Joint List and Ra’am). Note there are several different exit polls out from different TV channels. The exact numbers differ. But as far as I can tell they all agree on change bloc bigger, Likud single largest party. 17 or 18 seats for the two Arab parties, a historic high. In other words, this is more or less what polls have projected: an inconclusive result that makes it very unclear how either bloc can form a government. If neither can it means another election in the relatively near future. Again, though, final results can differ significantly from initial exit polls.

item.title: More On The Israeli Election
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: We’re coming up on the end of today’s voting in Israel. Historic high turnout is the story of the day. And I would say we still know basically nothing about the outcome. I’ve mentioned a couple times that prediction markets are really only good as distillations of conventional wisdom. But sometimes conventional wisdom can be good to know. On Kalshi today, we’ve seen a new possible prime minister rocketing from nowhere to a 39% probability of winning. And the new guy is “no one.”A few points on this. I’m a little surprised that “no one” wasn’t ranked higher before because while “no one” has maybe not been the most likely outcome there have been very good chances of his winning for weeks or months. Also remember that in case “no one” wins and no government can be formed, that actually means Netanyahu remains Prime Minister in a caretaker capacity while a new election is scheduled.Watching Israel Twitter there are various anti-Netanyahu politicians doing emergency messages, saying we’re behind, rush to the polls, etc. But this is what you say to get people out. And other signals point to equal amounts of desperation on both sides trying to get every last voter to the polls. Two other points to pay attention to.

item.title: There Is No Escaping Other Mommy
item.author: Defector Staff
item.content:encoded: There’s a Terry Pratchett quote I love, about how all contemporary fantasy is written under the influence of “Tolkien has become a sort of mountain, appearing in all subsequent fantasy in the way that Mt. Fuji appears so often in Japanese prints,” Pratchett wrote. “Sometimes it’s big and up close. Sometimes it’s a shape on the horizon. Sometimes it’s not there at all, which means that the artist either has made a deliberate decision against the mountain, which is interesting in itself, or is in fact standing on Mt. Fuji.”I think this holds true for all genre fiction; there are giants of the genre, who introduced basically all of the tropes, fully formed, and anyone working in that genre is constantly in conversation with those tropes. Every ghost story is in communion with Henry James; every haunted house owes a debt to Shirley Jackson. This isn’t necessarily a bad thing. Cliches become cliches for a reason, and it can be rewarding as a reader to spot the influences.We are primed to expect the expected, just by picking up a ghost story in the first place. “Ghost stories might not all use the same words,” Malerman has one of his characters observe, “but they all sound like the same words because it’s the ghost we think about, not the words.”

item.title: How The Best Moment Of Cheating In Soccer History Makes The Case Against VAR
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: What was your favorite video review controversy at this past summer's World Cup? Was it when Egypt had the best goal in their history disallowed for a foul committed by an unrelated guy 15 seconds before the big moment, when Iran lost to that same Egypt side over a totally fake offsides call, when the mouth-covering red card rule was applied against a Paraguayan player but not against an England player, or when Donald Trump personally lobbied FIFA to get a red card against Folarin Balogun rescinded? It's hard to choose from such a bounty of options. The 2026 World Cup represented a nadir in the evolution of soccer as theatrical product, with interminable replay reviews bringing the action to a halt in the name of adjudicating decisions that a referee couldn't possibly make. The world has been told that the death of theater is the price of fairness.I hate this stuff, especially because VAR is wrong all the time. The counterargument would be that without VAR, referees would miss even more stuff and that the world would see big, consequential calls get blown without the ability to review them. On this week's episode of , we examine the most famous missed call in the history of soccer as a way of making the argument against VAR. Our show is often accused of being pro-cheating, which is usually mistaking curiosity for endorsement. But in this case the charges are correct: We absolutely love the Hand of God.

item.title: Once Upon a Time in Harlem
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: The Harlem Renaissance was a cultural and intellectual movement of African-American artists in the 1920s and 30s. In 1972, filmmaker William Greaves threw a party in Duke Ellington’s apartment for some surviving members of the movement and recorded the whole thing. The footage sat unused for 50 years until Greaves’ son David picked up the project. The result is the documentary film, Once Upon a Time in Harlem; here’s the trailer.A decade after his death, genre-defying filmmaker William Greaves has one last trick up his sleeve with what he considered the most important event he captured on film: a 1972 party he engineered with the living luminaries of the Harlem Renaissance.For four hours, this extraordinary group – many of whom had not seen each other in fifty years – reminisced, critiqued, argued, laughed and drank while wrestling with their place in a rapidly shifting cultural landscape.Shot on 16mm film, newly restored and now directed by Greaves’ son David, this landmark film is at once a self-exploration and an inquiry into the heart of the critical mass of energy called the Harlem Renaissance.William Greaves’ intent was not only to document these artists and intellectuals as they spoke about their lives and work but also to plumb the meaning of the extraordinary creative period in which they lived to help us better understand how culture has been passed on from one generation to another and the role that the artist plays in keeping it alive.It looks fantastic. Once Upon a Time in Harlem currently has a 100% rating (67 reviews) on Rotten Tomatoes.

item.title: Paul Pierce Cries Poverty In Grim Men’s Court Documents
item.author: Chris Thompson
item.content:encoded: Paul Pierce claims he's having trouble making ends meet. The extraordinarily divorced Celtic great and occasional television bomb-out is paying a cumulative $48,000 per month in child and spousal support to at least two women, per court documents obtained and reported by TMZ. That is a lot of money. His ex-girlfriend Princess Santiago, with whom Pierce engaged in a public and nasty paternity dispute, is reportedly asking a court to award her another $40,000 in legal fees, and for $10,000 to hire a forensic accountant. She suspects that Pierce has been dishonest about his resources. Per TMZ, Pierce filed paperwork in response to this request, claiming that he is broke and "drowning" under his financial obligations.Some of Pierce's trouble comes from job instability. Pierce lost a well-paid ESPN gig in 2021 after posting selfie videos to social media from a profoundly grim house party. Pierce later insisted that he did not regret the tragic scene, or regret posting the video of it, and didn't really even regret losing his job at ESPN, a situation that he said had already become strained. It took him three years to land another network gig, but Pierce filled some of the time filming grim livestreams with Kevin Garnett in a deal with sports gambling outfit BetMGM. In March 2024, Pierce was brought on at Fox Sports 1 as a basketball analyst; per TMZ, his contract with FS1 paid him $1.5 million annually. He started as a contributor on Skip Bayless's ; when Bayless departed and folded, Pierce joined Joy Taylor and Keyshawn Johnson as co-hosts of the show . That also blew up, in July 2025, when Taylor was jettisoned and was cancelled.It seems like Pierce was still collecting some of this sweet FS1 income into this year, per documents from his latest divorce, reported by TMZ back in July. According to those documents, Pierce was hauling in about $165,000 per month for the first half of 2026, although some of this income was from various side deals; you know damn well Pierce was being paid by an online sportsbook.

item.title: The Harlem Renaissance Is Still Alive In ‘Once Upon A Time In Harlem’
item.author: Matene Toure
item.content:encoded: On a hot summer day in August 1972, actor-turned-documentarian William Greaves orchestrated a cocktail party at Duke Ellington’s home. He invited the surviving architects of the Harlem Renaissance and encouraged them to bask in impassioned discussion of the history and legacy of that period. Greaves, along with his son David and two other cameramen, captured 60,000 feet of film of the entire event. Throughout the remainder of his life and career, he wrestled with how to use the footage. At one point he hoped to use it in the award-winning documentary (1974), but instead decided to set it aside, giving it room to breathe. Greaves died in 2014 at the age of 87, with the raw footage still unfinished and fragmentary. His son, David, and granddaughter, Liani, then took up the mantle of this important restorative project. They were helped in this effort by Greaves’ widow, Louise Archambault Greaves, who preserved and safeguarded the archive with a grant from the Ford Foundation until her death in 2023. Shot on 16mm, Once Upon a Time in Harlem is a work of historical immersion animated by the very participants of one of the most influential eras in cultural history. Over the course of the documentary, the surviving members of a once-vibrant community of Black artists, poets, musicians, and writers from the 1920s—now senior citizens, dressed in their Sunday finest—recollect, reflect, and contest each other's memories and anecdotes of a period in which they not only lived but helped define. By interlacing the party scenes with other interviews conducted by William Greaves, archival material, literary texts, and cultural iconography, David resurrects the Renaissance period they all gathered to recall. Cinema becomes a vault for Black oral histories, to be passed down for generations to come. Born and raised in Harlem to a working-class Caribbean family, William Greaves grew up at the tail end of the Harlem Renaissance. At the behest of his religious parents, he was introduced to Black performance, poetry, culture, and radical histories. In his younger years, Greaves performed in African dance troupes. He later became interested in acting and worked with the American Negro Theater before transitioning into radio, television, and film. In an interview with the film scholar Scott MacDonald, Greaves recalls an epiphany about discovering the works of pioneering independent Black filmmaker Oscar Micheaux:

item.title: The Milwaukee Brewers Win At Everything
item.author: Kathryn Xu
item.content:encoded: In the top of the fifth inning of Monday's Game 3 of the World Series, Milwaukee captain Christian Yelich hustled into second base off a ground ball hit by William Contreras. He was called out on the field, ending the half-inning. The play looked well worth a challenge, but with two outs, I still decided that it would be a good time to take a shower. When I came out of the shower, the Brewers had scored eight two-out runs, extending their lead to 10-0. It went like this: single, single, double, double, single, double, flyout. Then the Rays just had to play through the rest of the game to get to the next one, where they will be fending off a sweep. https://youtu.be/y_06drhyWDI The first two games of the series showcased the Brewers' historic skillset as pesky fighters who never go away. Neither of their starters, Jacob Misiorowski and Logan Henderson, were at their best; Game 1 featured some uncharacteristic wobbles in the fundamentals from both teams, and Henderson gave up four runs in the first inning of Game 2. Each game featured some ninth-inning weirdness, with Game 1 ending after a video review and smoke on the field from some overeager celebratory fireworks, and Game 2 ending on an unreviewable checked-swing call with the top of the Tampa Bay lineup up to bat.

item.title: The Other Election
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: We’re most of the way through election day in Israel. The only thing we can say with certainty is that in the morning, voter turnout was the highest it had been since 1973. And now, coming into dinner time, it is the highest in all Israeli history. But we can’t really read anything clear into this: this is a high-stakes election for all the players. While I’d like to think it’s driven by a rejection of Netanyahu (and it could be), there’s no reason to think — based on this data point — that high turnout favors one side over another. As I noted earlier, the bulk of evidence suggests that Netanyahu’s bloc will come in “behind.” But that’s not really what matters. The question is whether the opposition bloc, if it gets more seats, can find a way to cobble together a coalition. That remains very uncertain. If no government can be formed, Netanyahu remains caretaker PM while another election is called.

item.title: The Heat Are Drowning
item.author: Luis Paez-Pumar
item.content:encoded: When the Miami Heat traded for Giannis Antetokounmpo this past summer, I started to imagine a fourth championship parade down Biscayne Boulevard. Here's a top-five player, a perennial MVP candidate, and he's coming to Miami. Wow, great, love it! Sure, the Heat gave up pretty much every asset it had aside from Bam Adebayo to make the trade work, and there were roster issues galore heading into the season, but still. Giannis! Antetokounmpo! How could this fail? It simply couldn't!Anyway, Miami lost to the Dallas Mavericks on Monday night and dropped to 0-4 for the season. Worse than that, the team has looked lost and overwhelmed in every single game. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=vDxNf1bBs6o

item.title: 3 Big Losses for Trump in One Long Day of Setbacks
item.author: David Kurtz
item.content:encoded: Yesterday was another extraordinary day on the political-legal front, with few commonalities among the three major rulings to knit them together into a coherent whole — except that the Trump administration consistently lost.Trump’s losses came across a wide-range of purported assertions of executive power. He was blocked from:interfering in California’s state-run federal elections;firing career federal prosecutor Maurene Comey in disregard of civil service protections; anddisregarding Congress and federal law in pushing forward his personalist golf course project in D.C.But set against those losses you still had corrupt new assertions of executive power:vindictively prosecuting Maurene Comey’s father, the former FBI director James Comey, for the time.You can see some connecting threads there, of course: the use of the Big Lie of noncitizen voting to undermine an election that Republicans are expected to lose badly, and the ongoing campaign of retribution against the Comey family for the supposed sins of the father.It is also implicitly a story of the federal judiciary stiffening its spine, albeit unevenly, in the face of outrageous conduct by the Trump administration both in and out of court.There’s a lot to unpack here, as the pace of Trump malfeasance quickens ahead of the election.Harmonic Convergence of Trump SchemesI do want to tie together two Trump schemes that have now become intertwined.For months, I’ve been banging on here about President Trump’s scheme to circumvent the Senate, the Constitution, and federal law to install loyalists as the top federal prosecutors in blue states.The scheme itself is lawless enough in its own right, but I’ve warned that it’s not an end unto itself, but a potential means to other bad acts, like targeting elected Dems.Now we’re seeing at least one aspect of the end game coming into view: election interference.Trump’s scheme to use the Big Lie of noncitizen voting to interfere in the midterm elections is being unspooled first in three districts that each have top federal prosecutors who were installed as part of Trump’s U.S. attorney scheme: the Central District of California and now the Eastern and Western Districts of Washington state.Both Bill Essayli in Los Angeles and Pete Serrano in Spokane were installed as top prosecutors via a backdoor workaround that courts in other districts have already shot down as unlawful. Charles Neil Floyd in Seattle was installed after Trump fired court-appointed U.S. Attorney Roger Rogoff (who is suing over his termination), another Trump DOJ method that other courts have already invalidated. In addition to Rogoff’s lawsuit, litigation has already been underway challenging the appointment of Essayli.Essayli has taken a high-profile public role in pushing the administration’s use of the pretext of noncitizen voting to interfere in the midterm elections. Serrano and Floyd followed suit yesterday with public fanfare. While the Big Lie scheme is being driven by top political appointees at Main Justice, all three prosecutors have made public pronouncements, and Essayli has facilitated arrests and prosecutions of alleged noncitizen voters.It’s harder to imagine pulling off the scheme to interfere in the midterms with independent U.S. attorneys in place who came into office in the usual lawful ways: either Senate-confirmed after blue-slip approval from home state Democratic senators, or as career first assistant U.S. attorneys, or as federal court appointees.The different lawful ways of installing a permanent or acting U.S. attorney speak to the checks and balances in place to preserve the separation of powers, pitting the legislative and judicial branches against the executive branch in a purposeful tension.Trump has run roughshod over those checks and balances, and while the courts have repeatedly rejected his U.S. attorney scheme, they’ve been too slow to prevent the scheme from having real-world impacts on the election.9th Circuit Blocks CA Election InterferenceIn a major early ruling, the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals rejected the Trump DOJ’s scheme to make California segregate and not count mail-in ballots from alleged noncitizen voters.The 2-1 decision, which I write about at length here, found the Trump DOJ appeal to be premature and left the court without appellate jurisdiction to even hear it. But the dissent by a Trump appointee who reached the merits of the case prompted the two judges in the majority to file separate concurrences that said they would have ruled against the Trump DOJ had they had jurisdiction.The two concurring opinions did two things: (i) laid out a map for the trial judge who is now considering the merits of the case what the appeals court panel will tolerate; and (ii) signaled to the Trump DOJ that it will be unlikely to prevail when the case returns to the 9th Circuit on the merits.Notably, neither the Trump DOJ or any other judge on the 9th Circuit sought a rehearing last night of the panel’s decision. Unless the Trump DOJ goes to the Supreme Court next (and a clearly premature appeal would be a terrible posture from which to seek high court intervention), the case resumes today with an important hearing in front of U.S. District Judge David O. Carter, who is in the somewhat unusual position of first taking up a case after it’s already been up on appeal.California Case Gets Even WackierAhead of today’s hearing in Los Angeles, the Trump DOJ filed new declarations overnight. Two things jump out, and they’re both doozies:The Trump DOJ filed a declaration in support of its case from none other than Clint Curtis, the top election official in Shasta County who offered a job in his office to Big Lie aficionado Tina Peters after she was released from prison in Colorado. Peters declined the job. Curtis, who was defeated for reelection in June by someone he fired, claims that based on his knowledge of county election systems Los Angeles County can easily segregate alleged noncitizen ballots as the Trump DOJ is demanding.In the course of challenging Los Angeles County’s preliminary analysis of the DOJ’s list of alleged noncitizen voter, a DHS official’s declaration appears to concede that one of the voters on the DOJ list turned out to be deceased and that four others “might have a claim to U.S. citizenship.”The Trump DOJ’s attempt to block the certification of the U.S. Senate election in Alaska sits in a different bucket than the Big Lie of noncitizen voting. This is an opportunistic effort to salvage a seat based on the potential confusion around two candidates names, one of whom is the incumbent Republican — but it has the usual hallmarks of Trump DOJ lawlessness and sloppiness.The state of Alaska defendants have responded to the DOJ’s lawsuit for the first time and are opposing it. They filed a motion to dismiss.Chief Judge Sharon L. Gleason (Obama) granted a motion to expedite her ruling on whether to allow Alaskans for Mary, the Democratic Senatorial Campaign Committee, and other third parties to intervene in the case. She set a briefing schedule on that motion and, in the event she allows them to intervene, on the intervenor’s motions to dismiss.In her order, Judge Gleason put enough spin on the ball to suggest she’s skeptical of the DOJ’s case. Among the clues she dropped, Judge Gleason noted that the general election ballot layout is the same as the one used in the primary and then wryly remarked: “The Court is unaware of any legal challenge as to how either candidate was listed on the primary ballot.”Judge Gleason also offered up this accurate but hardly neutral description of how we got here: “After Alaskans had already begun casting their ballots for the November 2026 election—and nearly four months after the Alaska Supreme Court directed the Division of Elections to include Daniel J. Sullivan on the ballot for the upcoming United States Senate election—the United States initiated this action on October 22, 2026.”The Biggest Pre-Election ConcernThere is a dangerous possibility that the California and Alaska lawsuits may be precursors for a search warrant to seize ballots. The federal government has relied on debunked claims of voter fraud in past ballot seizures, like in Fulton County. Given DOJ’s recent track record, the lack of evidence of any actual crime in Alaska or California may not deter the federal government in seeking a warrant.Trump Offers $1M for Voter Fraud TipsPresident Trump, in a social media post: “Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud!”“This is the first time ever that we have had to engage in scenario planning to safeguard against potential federal interference in elections. It seems like the federal government is now adversarial to the states.”—Shenna Bellows (D), Maine secretary of stateComey Vindictively Prosecuted AgainWrongfully Fired Maurene Comey WinsIn a case with big implications for civil service protections and for President Trump’s unlawful purge of the Justice Department, U.S. District Judge Jesse M. Furman of Manhattan ruled in favor of fired career federal prosecutor Maurene Comey in her wrongful termination lawsuit against the DOJ. Another case we could spend all day unpacking. Suffice to say that there’s a lot here that will be tested on appeal. Stay tuned …A Wild Ruling on Trump’s Golf Course PlanMost of the headlines are focused on U.S. District Judge Ana Reyes of D.C. blocking the Trump administration from cutting down any more trees on the East Potomac Golf Course, but the underlying issues are quite a bit more important than tree removal.Reyes’ ruling in the case also sets the stage for possible sanctions against the administration and in particular against Trump DOJ attorneys for their conduct in the case, including possibly misleading the court.If you have a few extra moments today, the first 6 1/2 pages of Reyes ruling are a tour de force that provide a very good sense of how off the rails things have gotten.

item.title: The American Divide on Empathy
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: PRRI’s 2026 American Values Survey reveals some, uh, interesting views on whether Americans think empathy is a good thing or not. Those respondents unaffiliated with a religion were much more inclined to think that empathy is “a foundational moral value that helps build a healthy society”.With the exception of white evangelical Protestants (42%), around two-thirds or more of all major religious groups believe that empathy is a foundational moral value for a healthy society, including about eight in ten religiously unaffiliated Americans (83%), members of other non-Christian religions (80%), and Jewish Americans (77%). By contrast, a majority of white evangelical Protestants (54%) believe empathy can become dangerous when it leads people away from building a society guided by God’s truth.Here’s the breakdown by party:(Btw, “not strongly agree” seems to mean “agree, but not strongly” and not “disagree”. Grammatically correct but a little confusing if you don’t read it carefully…)

item.title: More Like A Colossal Piece Of Shit
item.author: Sabrina Imbler
item.content:encoded: The story begins with a man fixated on the idea of a German shepherd, which was first bred for its wolf-like appearance and obedience as a worker. He is less invested in the dog as an animal as he is in the dog as a symbol of loyalty and obedience, always valuable traits under an authoritarian regime. He is also interested in tinkering with the dogs to hone them as weapons of war.I am speaking, of course, of the American entrepreneur Ben Lamm, one of the founders of the new defense technology company Warhound, which has raised $200 million in funding to create genetically modified dogs for the U.S. military, and law enforcement. The promotional art for Warhound is laughably fascist, featuring several German shepherds garbed like Tier 1 operators. They wear tactical vests and protective sunglasses and helmets. Two of the dogs are totally white for reasons that are unclear but also unsettling.I've written about Lamm before, and the gripes I have with his most famous startup, Colossal Biosciences, which has raised hundreds of millions of dollars in ostensible pursuit of its promise to "de-extinct" the mammoth and other flashy prehistorics, despite being dishonest about what "de-extinction" really means. Although I did not predict Colossal's next outlandish project would rise to the bar of "genetically modified murder dogs," I can't say I'm surprised. In classic Colossal fashion, these war dogs do not exist yet. Also in classic Colossal fashion, the company has promised a short timeline: puppies early next year and dogs in military service in two years.
