item.title: I’m so fucking tired of this election cycle
item.author: Jeff Tiedrich
item.source: everyone is entitled to my own opinion
item.content:encoded: Once again, these fucking fucks have me completely fucking exhausted. Every morning is like, ‘oh my god, what stupid shit are they going to pull today?’It’s all so eternally . The relentless barrage of flimsy lies. The flop-sweat desperation of losing losers who know they’re going to lose. The nonstop bigotry, misogyny, transphobia and Islamophobia of d-list demagogues trying to terrify people into voting for them.And it just keeps on getting stupider.Do we all really have to endure the next seven days? Can’t we just magically skip ahead to next Wednesday, when we all wake up into a world where the fuckfaces have lost?Anybody reporting Voter Fraud in the past Elections, or the upcoming 2026 Midterm Election, will be paid $1,000,000 upon the arrest and conviction of those that created the Fraud! Thank you for your attention to this matter. President DONALD J. TRUMPJesus H. Christ on a cockeyed catamaran, are you kidding me with this nonsense? It’s just one cheesy after another with this imbecile. How many times has Dear Leader tried to bribe the morons into voting for him? First he promised that everyone would get a check for five grand if Republicans won the midterms. Next, he promised to bestow a 1% bounty on anyone who blew the whistle on corporate fraud. Of course this penny-ante con artist has no intention of following through on any of his worthless promises, but try explaining that to the cultists. And now, this latest lie, the vow to fork over a cool mil to anyone who roots out That’s all I need, some vigilante dipshit in a MAGA hat, skulking about my polling place, while I’m trying to fill out my ballot. He’s there because Dear Leader promised him ONE MILLION DOLLARS.Go the fuck home, dumb-ass. You’ve fallen for it again. You’re not getting shit from Dear Leader, and you’re just getting in everyone’s way.“There’s five hundred million Arabs in the world. And yet they don't produce science. They don’t win the Nobel Prize. They don’t win the Fields Prize. They don’t win the Wolf Prize. They don’t produce literature.”Could the Marvelous Mister Measles please stop gargling with the Drano? Where is Bobby Brainworms Jr getting his information? This isn’t even racism. It’s ignorant bullshit. For fuck’s sake, dude went to Harvard. Didn’t he learn anything while there, aside from the best kind of toilet seat to snort coke off of? It’s a legit question to ask, because Brainworms, you’ll be shocked to hear, is spewing complete nonsense.Do you know why our modern orthographic system of numbers are called ‘Arabic numerals’? It’s because the Arabs that shit. If it weren’t for what some Arab dude named Muhammad ibn Musa al-Khwarizmi worked out , right now we’d be dicking around with trying to figure out the square root of MCXXVIII. Good luck with that, hotshot. Instead of denigrating Arabs, Bobby Brainworms should go thank one.Around 9 to 12 Arabs or individuals of direct Arab origin/nationality have won Nobel Prizes, depending on how “Arab” is defined (such as including the diaspora or specific national origins). [1, 2]Prominent Arab laureates include Nobel Peace Prize winners Anwar Sadat (Egypt, 1978), Yasser Arafat (Palestine, 1994), Mohamed ElBaradei (Egypt, 2005, jointly with the IAEA), Tawakkol Karman (Yemen, 2011), and Nadia Murad (Iraq, 2018) for their peacebuilding and human rights efforts. In science and literature, laureates include Naguib Mahfouz (Egypt, 1988, Literature) and Ahmed Zewail (Egypt, 1999, Chemistry). [1, 2, 3] Where’s rinky-dink award?“Gas prices are too high ... they skyrocket every time some tinpot dictator decides to throw a tantrum.”Hang on there — did Couchfuck just blunder into committing an honesty?Because he’s right. There is one tinpot dictator in particular, who, every time he opens his rancid anus-mouth, causes the price of to skyrocket. You know who I’m talking about.Bro, Donny’s going throw a massive shit-fit when he discovers you’ve been trash-talking him to a half-dozen MAGA jamokes in some high-school gymnasium.Couchfuck so terrible at this. If I were a Republican candidate, and they told me that Mr. Heartbeat Away was coming to campaign for me, I’d change the locks and pretend I wasn’t home.I’m so fucking tired of every one of these shit-weasels contriving to escape accountability.Check out Piss-Drunk Pete Kegstand, our butt-dialing Secretary of Death. He knows that the long knives are out for him. He knows that if the Dems retake Congress, he’s right up top of the list of fucksticks who are going to get the shit impeached out of them.Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth is reportedly “angling” for a Senate seat over fears House Democrats plan to launch an impeachment investigation into his tenure after the midterms.According to Puck, the secretary is interested in succeeding Tennessee’s incumbent Republican Sen. Marsha Blackburn should she win her race to be the state’s next governor against Democratic rival Jerri Green, as she is currently on course to do.Oh great, in the event of Tennessee Senator Marsha Bag-of-Hair becoming Governor Bag-Of-Hair, Piss-Drunk Pete is going to pester her until she hands him her old job, thereby weaseling out of being impeached for being absolute shit at Oh yeah, that’ll be awesome. Can you imagine the dumbfuckery that Piss-Drunk Pete could get up into, if he were to become the Esteemed Senator Kegstand? He could fire all the fatties and the beardos among his Senate staffers. I’m sure there’s some irreplaceable historic globe somewhere in the halls of the Capitol Building he can drunkenly trip over and destroy.Oh, and he can demand to check the t-levels of Mitch McConnell.Let’s hope that Piss-Drunk Pete’s plan to do an end-run around accountability works out as well as his plan to not flip a skateboard up into his own nuts. It’s all so exhausting. Isn’t there some way to avoid this? Can’t we all just vote early, and then ourselves through the next seven days, waking up into a better world? Wouldn’t that be fucking awesome?Yeah, but then we’d miss seven days of the Daily Claudia. That would Today, let’s have some covid-era fun. First up, it’s in the back yard with Tenchi the Wonder Cat, on June 3, 2020.Next, chilling by the woodshed, on April 4, 2020.And, lastly, kinda-sorta socially distancing down at the lake with Scott, Kathy and Adela, on June 21, 2020.Have a great Tuesday, everyone! here’s your daily reminder that I can be found on Blue Sky at this link.this is going to be my closing message for the foreseeable future: do what you need to do to keep sane. if that means you need to disengage with my daily posts for a while, I get it. this community of ours will still be here when you return.to all the people who have signed on in the days since the election, . settle in as we all try to deal with the shitfuckery that’s ahead of us.we are all in this together, and we are all here for each other.

item.title: Signal your virtues
item.content:encoded: is often used as an insult, but it’s to signal your virtues, actually.A few months back, I read a story on Bluesky from a hispanic woman who’s immigrant mother got lost in the city. Her phone ran of battery, she didn’t speak much English, and she had no idea how to get home.She approached a young woman with bright blue hair who was able to use her phone’s translation app to get the mother’s address and help her get home.When the daughter asked how she knew she could trust that person—as an immigrant in a country like the US in these scary times—she said “because of her blue hair.”I recently had a conversation with a hispanic friend of mine about this, and he mentioned that progress flags, “all are welcome here” signs, and so on let his family know they’re safe in an area.It got me thinking about how important—essential even—virtue signaling is.To that end, I decided to get backpack and sew some fun patches on it. I’m bald AF, so dying my hair is out. I tried painting my nails recently. It was a fucking disaster! And I need a backpack for transporting groceries with my bike anyways.While I found myself gravitating towards “eat the rich” and “punch nazis” type patches, I decided to go with mostly ones that spread more joy instead.Looking at them, I don’t think there’s any doubt what my political leanings are.They let vulnerable people know they’re safe with me. And just as importantly, they let the wrong kind of people know they’re not.I bought all of my patches on Etsy from (hopefully?) Indie shops.The Progress Flag patch is even more vivid in real life than it looks in the photo. It’s also thick as hell, and took to sew on!I take my backpack with me basically everywhere, now, so this gets a lot of use!

item.title: Mark Teixeira Is Sleepwalking Into Congress
item.author: Alex Shultz
item.content:encoded: During his 14-year MLB career, Mark Teixeira’s average Wins Above Replacement (WAR) was a respectable 4.4. As a political candidate, Teixeira’s WAR—yes, there’s a platform that measures this sort of thing, and yes, he’s running for office—might very well be the inverse.It is very likely that Teixeira will soon become the representative for Texas’ 21st congressional district. If he receives this honor, he will do so without putting any meaningful effort into his campaign. Teixeira is a carpetbagger who only recently moved close to, not even within the boundaries of, the district he hopes to represent. His assets portfolio presents endless conflicts of interest. He has zero political experience except for helping push through a school vouchers program so toxic and unpopular that it’s imperiling Texas Governor Greg Abbott’s re-election bid. The “issues” page of his campaign website reads like it was written by ChatGPT 1.0. In interviews, he’s struggled to convey basic policy positions or express why he’s running. The best he could muster to Sean Hannity is that, in 30 or 40 years, he hopes his children look back and say they’re glad their dad “stood up for capitalism and for our free-market economy and for freedom.”The one thing Teixeira has going for him is that he was great at hitting home runs. Teixeira’s 409 dingers won him celebrity status and landed him the endorsements of Gov. Abbott and President Trump; those endorsements have provided a huge cushion in Texas’s deep-red 21st congressional district, which includes a handful of rural counties and the northern portion of San Antonio. In March, during a crowded primary to fill the soon-to-be-vacated seat of Rep. Chip Roy, Teixeira secured an overwhelming 60.9 percent of the vote, enough to avoid a runoff.

item.title: Inches & Miles
item.author: Ernie Smith
item.source: Tedium: The Dull Side of the Internet.
item.content:encoded: The AI era seems to be emboldening startups to once again take bold swings and use your data without even bothering to ask so they can build a startup around it.It’s the great truism of the internet: You give an inch, and folks will take a mile.Back when I was running ShortFormBlog in 2009, I remember trying a number of digital startups, all of which promised different ways to help monetize my content through optimization or some clever feature that made my site 5% better. These scripts were mostly horrible, with the exception of Apture, humane tech advocate Tristan Harris’ startup. I eventually got rid of most of them as I quickly realized what they were doing. But most of them had an underlying goal: They wanted my audience’s data.The most notable example of this was Facebook’s Like button, perhaps the most infamous bait-and-switch conducted by the company before the pivot to video. The company convinced websites large and small to put a little code on their page in exchange for a chance at traffic. (And worse, they wouldn’t let you customize the damn thing to match the look of your site, so it looked ugly as sin.) But what was actually happening was two things: Facebook had created a massive dragnet of data on its users by making random websites a part of its network, and it was setting the stage for a lot of people to eventually shut down their external website and stay on Facebook. For better or worse, it changed online culture forever.The external Like button died earlier this year, having served its purpose. Now, if you want to link your own website on one of those Facebook pages you quickly linked back to, you have to pay Facebook money. I’m not kidding.I’ve been thinking a lot about this era, which brought us chumboxes and ever-intrusive ads, because it kind of feels like what’s starting to happen with AI.Case in point: Over the weekend, I got an email from an AI company that wanted me to link their product. Not exactly unique these days. But what was unique was that it was essentially a form letter from a service called Listaify, which appeared to be a middleman that promised to get platforms to link your little startup.I did some research on this and what I found was that Listaify had put me on their site, informing audiences that I was “accepting AI tools.” Now, if you read my prior post about these AI-based submissions, you probably know that I was not exactly raring to promote every AI product under the sun. Much the opposite. But this company had gone out of its way to describe my posting habits, what I was willing to accept and not accept, and my apparent reach. (But apparently, they had missed the part where I got iLands to add unsubscribe links to their AI bots by drawing attention to their bad behavior.)Put another way, this company scraped my data. That’s bad.But here’s what’s worse: This company not only tries to shove links into my inbox at a time when a lot of companies are shoving links into my inbox, but it has turned it into a business. It essentially encourages startups to pay them hundreds or even thousands of dollars per year to help you promote your tools on various blogs and platforms.This sucks—it is a systematic strategy to wear bloggers down to promote AI tools, even if it’s not their focus. Plus, by placing themselves in the middle of the relationship, they’re taking potential advertising revenue from outlets that could use it. This is not why I got into blogging nearly 20 years ago, and it’s not why I’m going to do it now.Services like these exploit founders and creators by attempting to optimize everything to within an inch of its life, and it does more harm to the ecosystem than help. This is not uncommon with PR pitches, but it feels like every decision I make, every word I write on my site is a data point for someone else to exploit readers.If you use this service, at least when it comes to Tedium, you are wasting your money. (In fact I updated my contribute page to forbid it.) If you want to support independent journalism, don’t exploit it.(I will note, to their credit, that when I complained, they removed me. But there was no apology, no recognition that their attempt to push even more AI projects into my inbox might be unwelcome.)But they’re not the only example of take-an-inch-give-a-mile philosophy I’m seeing creep up in a big way. Recently, I recently got a series of LinkedIn messages from a person running an adtech platform. He informed me that he had gathered all my past sponsor info to fill his database and was willing to give me access to it for free. I felt uncomfortable about the fact that he just took my data and was essentially trying to offer it back to me, and so (after thinking it over for a while), I told him to remove my information from his platform. Despite being so desperate to get my attention previously, he never replied.I understand the nature of scraping of public data. It can be done in responsible ways. (And yes, it’s likely that your info has been scraped thousands of times in the decades since the internet took off.) And scraping is probably going to be an important part of the future of the internet. But in both of these cases, companies I never heard of tried to insert themselves into my business. And in both cases, I had to point out that I had not given them permission to do so.Companies like these take an inch and give a mile. And they’re far from alone. There’s no ethics to it. It’s take-an-inch-give-a-mile across the board. It’s what eventually leads people to stop giving inches.The internet, ignoring the gatekeeping, was built on a collective sense of altruism. People helping out other people. It’s why Craigslist exists, after all. But it just takes a few bad actors to ruin the whole thing, which means that it was arguably spoiled long ago. And as these examples highlight, there are more bad actors than ever.I don’t want the internet to be a gatekeepery scene again. But they’re making it hard.To Nevada, the 3-year-old that’s so good at soccer that someone called the cops on him: That’s a horrible thing to go through, but I can’t wait until everyone knows your name.As celebrity music projects go, Dead Man’s Bones is pretty much one of the best ones ever. Ryan Gosling was a B+-list actor when it came out, and almost immediately after, he jumped up to the A+ list. So it’s no wonder that his very good Halloween-themed rock band, whose 2009 album notably featured a choir, stayed dormant for 17 years. No longer: They just released a brand-new song this week.Find this one an interesting read? Share it with a pal! And back it it (with some Halloween-themed stuff) later this week.By the way, help support us by checking out the weird crap at the Tedium Shopping Network. At least you know what you’re getting into there.

item.title: It's not the bots, Flock
item.author: Samantha Cole
item.content:encoded: Flock CEO Garrett Langley says some interesting things to cops behind closed doors. He about his surveillance technology’s role in tracking a woman who had self-administered an abortion and 404 Media’s coverage of that incident, calling it “entirely false.” Now, in leaked audio obtained by 404 Media, Langley is saying the protests that have broken out around the country against his company, many of which have resulted in communities canceling their contracts with Flock and bagging up the cameras, are not real. Seems pretty real to me! Garrett Langley, the CEO of automatic license plate reader company Flock, told an audience of police chiefs at a private police conference Sunday that anti-Flock protests around the country are not real, according to leaked audio obtained by 404 Media.He also said his wife advised him to never apologize, said he would prefer to never do interviews with the press again, and claimed without evidence that the social media opposition to Flock is driven mostly by Russian bots.“Somebody was paying for [the social media posts and] stopped paying for it,” Langley said about the many viral posts criticizing his company’s technology. “Social media chatter on Flock is down about 95 percent from July. It went down 50 percent last week when Ukraine bombed a Russian data center with a drone. Literally 50 percent overnight. And so look, SI’m the last person, my wife as well, she’s like ‘This is crazy, these people are getting paid to say these things,’” he added, repeating a disproven theory that Ukraine’s strikes on Russian data centers had a significant impact on internet bot activity. “It’s anonymous bots, and so it is not real,” he continued. “Inorganic activity has led to organic activity, but when I look at protests across the country, it is the same people with the same signs and the same message. That’s not normal. That’s not organic at all.” Langley’s comments echo another unsubstantiated theory that said opposition to Flock comes from a far-left network spreading propaganda at the behest of China.Apple’s $2,000 folding phone, the iPhone Duo, came out just two days ago and people are already seeing big fat creases down the middle of the folding screen, and some devices are cracked in the same specific spot too. People waited in line overnight at Apple stores to get this thing, and now we’re seeing photos of heinous cracked and creased-up Duos all over social media. In some cases, the phone screens have cracked along the crease, causing a crashout people are now calling “crackgate.” Bold choice. Let’s see if it pays off. Proton, the company behind ProtonMail and other privacy-focused products, told staff on Monday it would be ‘re-interviewing’ staff across the company about how they use AI in their jobs, with the implication that the interviews may decide whether staffers have “continued employment,” according to an internal Proton email obtained by 404 Media. “These re-interviews are consequential,” a part of the email reads. “Interviewers will document their assessments, which will inform the broader review of our organization and talent. That review may lead to changes in roles, responsibilities, and continued employment. Individual outcomes will be communicated directly once decisions are finalized.”Are we living in the same timeline? In Sunday’s edition of the , Marissa Mayer, former president and CEO of Yahoo, told her interviewer something so absurd it’s since gone viral. Struggling with the “impossible task” of naming three things that she loves about her own 10 year old daughter, the New York Times reports, Mayer asked the AI assistant she just launched to do that thinking for her. What she has to say about gender in tech, however, is more out of touch than that. The rest of the story gets into something Mayer has talked about for more than a decade: “the gender card,” as she’s called it. She’s been asked about gender in tech one million times, and has mostly dismissed it. But a decade after the tech girlboss reigned, her thoughts on this haven’t seemed to evolve much.I am obsessed with the phrase “catty patty.” Catfish, a criminally underrated Eastern Shore delicacy, makes an appearance in NPR. I’ve only ever known catfish as a very annoying sucker to get on the line, and a pretty good fried fish. Apparently they’re fucking with the ecosystem, so it’s time to eat ‘em. I will do my part. Muse is targeting older adults. And Meta knows it. : “‘And the more Siobhán got to know me, the more Siobhán was able to give me what I wanted,’ Fay says, referring to the name she gave the agent, a nod to her Irish heritage. Meta encourages its users to name their AIs—and encourages its AIs to think like humans. ‘You are not a chatbot,’ Muse’s internal instructions read. ‘You are becoming someone.’”Dictionary.com just named the word "maxxing" as its 2026 Word of the Year. Its definition: "A word that refers to the practice of pursuing an activity to the fullest or optimizing a certain aspect of your life." is the Wikipedia for things within a mile and a half of you. I know what I’m doing after work today.

item.title: We’re dropping the paywall
item.author: 1axbl21ntx88nwmi3l338rjqhqyk6oxtgxf89f@bf56x.hubspotemail.net
item.content:encoded: Last night, during an interview on MS NOW, Jen Psaki noted that I seemed calmer and “more Zen” about the challenges facing our elections. “I’m just tired,” I corrected her.With a week until the midterms, the attacks on our elections are coming fast and furious. Most disturbingly, they are being funded by U.S. taxpayers and carried out by government lawyers.The law firm I chair, Elias Law Group, is fighting in 43 states to protect your right to vote. We are litigating more than 90 lawsuits and are battling the DOJ in more than 30 cases.Yet fighting in court isn’t enough.The last few years have taught us that we also need to educate and inform the public about these attacks and how they are being defeated. I created Democracy Docket in 2020 to do just that.From the beginning, I have had to balance free access with the need to offer premium members exclusive content. It has not always been easy to decide what goes in which category.But over the weekend, I decided that between now and the election, Democracy Docket is dropping its paywall. This was not an easy decision.Some on the team agreed; others worried about the drop in new membership sign-ups that will likely result. I just don’t think we can withhold important information and analysis in these critical days.There are three cases everyone should be focused on right now.In Alaska, Trump’s DOJ is suing to block certification of the Senate election if Democrat Mary Peltola wins. The lawsuit is ridiculous and baseless. It never should have been filed.It was filed because Trump is desperate to steal a Senate seat he sees slipping away, along with the GOP majority. When asked about the case and why it was filed, he answered, “I’m the one that said do it.”My law firm has already moved to intervene on behalf of Peltola’s campaign and the DSCC. Late yesterday, the court agreed to expedite consideration of our motion to join the case and our motion to dismiss it. We will fight tooth and nail to protect Alaskan voters from this gross attack on their elections.Meanwhile, in California, the DOJ continues to hammer away at election officials and voters. Last week, the department sent letters to counties across California demanding they set aside mail ballots from alleged noncitizens and threatening election officials with potential criminal charges if they fail to comply.This is just the latest escalation of the Trump administration’s sweeping attack on California’s elections. On Sunday, the Ninth Circuit Court of Appeals held an emergency hearing on the DOJ’s claim that California must stop counting ballots from more than 20,000 people the federal government alleges are “likely” noncitizens.Yesterday, the court rejected this effort, dismissing the DOJ’s appeal. The majority noted that the DOJ’s emergency was largely of its own making.In a few hours, the case will return to the trial court for a hearing. My firm has moved to intervene on behalf of two nonprofit groups to protect the rights of voters and free and fair elections.Shortly before the court of appeals ruled, Trump’s DOJ demanded that Washington state set aside ballots from more than 400 voters it claims are noncitizens. This proves that whether you live in California or Nevada, Alaska or Michigan, Washington state or Washington, D.C., your vote is not safe.Put simply, if we don’t stop the DOJ in its tracks, it will use this playbook nationwide.That is why perhaps the most important case to watch is one my law firm is litigating in federal court in Washington, D.C., on behalf of the DSCC, DCCC, DGA and Nevada Democratic Party, as well as Senator Schumer and Congressman Jeffries. In that case, we are seeking to block the Trump administration from threatening state election officials with criminal prosecution and pressuring states to deny ballots to registered voters.Trump and his allies are using intimidation and coercion to dictate who can vote and how elections are run. My law firm is working to end their pressure campaign, and we will not stop until every American’s vote is protected.Democracy Docket is here to keep you informed and armed with accurate information. That is why I decided to drop the paywall.To be clear, it is Democracy Docket premium members who make this possible. They stand with us every day in defense of free and fair elections.Premium members receive my exclusive analysis and invitations to special events. Most of all, they help ensure Democracy Docket has the resources to thrive and grow at this critical time.

item.title: Marissa Mayer Can’t Keep Pretending 'Gender Doesn't Matter'
item.author: Samantha Cole
item.content:encoded: In Sunday’s edition of the, Marissa Mayer, former president and CEO of Yahoo, told her interviewer something so absurd it’s since gone viral. Struggling with the “impossible task” of naming three things that she loves about her own 10 year old daughter, , Mayer asked the AI assistant she just launched to do that thinking for her. It delivered the perfect answer, Mayer said: “It came back and was like, your daughter is empathetic, creative and an animal lover.” Everyone is piling onto that absurd anecdote right now, rightfully so. What she has to say about gender in tech, however, is more out of touch than that.Saying sensational things on the record — especially knowing that the reporter will not be able to resist using such a shocking story as the lede — is a savvy strategy. For someone as influential as Mayer, telling the list story is transparently a result of years of media training. Mayer is selling her new app, Dazzle, which accesses your camera roll and analyzes your life based on the photos you take. It’s disturbing to see her talk about relinquishing basic cognitive skills like “plan a birthday party” to AI. But the rest of the story gets into something Mayer has talked about for more than a decade: “the gender card,” as she’s called it. “I never play the gender card,” she told Steven Levy . “The moment you play into that, it’s an issue. [...] In technology we live at a rare, fast-moving pace. There are probably industries where gender is more of an issue, but our industry is not one where I think that’s relevant.” She repeats similar sentiments in Sunday’s NYT interview.The height of Mayer’s career coincided with the girlbossification of everything, during the era, when Notorious RBG and “well behaved women rarely make history” mugs were everywhere. She’s been asked about gender in tech one million times, and has mostly dismissed it. But a decade after the tech girlboss reigned, her thoughts on this haven’t seemed to evolve much. Later in the NYT piece, she brushed off the notion that gender has any bearing on who gets to participate in the tech industry. She also brushes off a question about bias baked into AI models, something that’s been and , and instead names female AI executives like Fei-Fei Li as the reason well-documented bias doesn’t exist. She asserts that passion overrides gender, as if just being “passionate” enough erases decades of women’s experiences in the tech workforce. “To me, gender fades into the background. I talk about passion as a gender neutralizing force,” she told the NYT. “If you’re excited about something, gender doesn’t matter.”Meanwhile, male figureheads of the AI industry are out here posting on main. leave the industry by 35, earn 84 cents to their male counterparts’ dollar, and women founders receive half the amount of funding that male founders do.Earlier this month, event organizers canceled one of the biggest gatherings of women and non-binary technologists, the Grace Hopper Celebration. “Unlike past events, this year, both individual registrations and sponsorship commitments came in significantly below our expectations and, ultimately, below the level needed to cover critical operating expenses,” the organizers wrote in a statement. that this comes after years of declining attendance, with around 15,000 people attending in 2025, making it the fewest since 2016. In 2023, standing in lines for hours to talk to recruiters, being shoved, harassed, and cut in front of by the hundreds of men who’d suddenly flooded the conference. “They trampled over attendees, shoved their way into the recruiter’s booth to wave their resumes in front of their faces, verbally assaulted attendees, and physically pushed and shoved attendees in line,” one attendee said. After the GHC 2026 cancellation was announced, Kayley Seow, a tech worker who was at the 2023 conference, contacted me to talk about what it meant to her. She said she felt “pretty shattered” when she heard the conference wouldn’t happen this year. “GHC is such a pillar of the community that you don't expect to fall, or in this case, not run. Despite its flaws, it continues to be an important space for people hoping to get into tech and those already in it. I'd been recommending it to every undergrad or woman technologist to attend.” There are other, similar conferences held around the country, but GHC is hard to recreate, Seow told me. “Other organizations exist but they operate virtually, there's events here and there in the Bay, but it's impossible to find something as concentrated as GHC.” The people she knows who are most affected are current undergrads who planned to go to GHC to connect with recruiters, find internships, and land graduate jobs, Seow said. “They're disappointed, and a little scared, since it's October and we're coming up on the end of internship recruiting season, especially for the international students who were hoping to talk to the bigger companies at GHC that have the resources to take on international students as interns.” It’s still unclear whether there will be a conference in 2027.GHC’s cancellation this year follows a string of blows to organizations that support women technologists. Women Who Code, a nonprofit that awarded more than $3.5 million in scholarships and supported a community of 360,000 members, after 11 years, citing funding issues. Things are very different today than they were when Mayer was the first-ever pregnant CEO of a Fortune 500 company. In 2025, at the direction of President Donald Trump’s executive order “Ending Radical and Wasteful Government DEI Programs and Preferencing” and other orders, civil servants across the federal government to the Social Security office and the CDC had to drop everything to scrub mentions of diversity, equity and inclusion from their systems. This wasn’t just symbolic or semantic. The National Institutes of Health terminated billions of dollars worth of nearly 2,300 federal research grants, cuts that disproportionately affected women and early career researchers. Led entirely by inexperienced men in their early 20s and spearheaded by Elon Musk, the now-defunct Department of Government Efficiency that would have advanced potentially lifesaving research projects focused on pregnancy and reproductive health, chronic illness, and vaccine safety for women. The damage done by DOGE cuts to the advancement of science and technology that would have been done by women and would have improved women’s lives around the world is immeasurable and widespread; it’s hard to imagine believing gender plays no role in STEM today in light of what we have seen under the Trump administration over the last year and a half, especially.But in a way, Mayer is right: Drinking one’s own Kool-Aid is a non-gendered issue. Earlier this year, AI generating podcasts to interact with your kids about their days and got similarly roasted for a week straight. He deserved it, and so does she.

item.title: This Ad Has All the Internet Nostalgia
item.author: Miss Cellania
item.content:encoded: In the early days of this millennia, the internet was a delightful playground of nonsense. That was back before everything turned political, there was no AI slop, scams were fewer, and monetization really wasn't much of a thing. Even bots and trolls were just a minor annoyance. The World Wide Web was full of people who just wanted to share a laugh and show off their creativity. An ad for Firefox takes us back to those days by resurrecting the biggest viral memes of the early internet, from Numa Numa to Chuck Testa. Beware, some of these folks have aged, especially the kids, so this compilation may make you feel old. If you show this to your children or grandchildren, you'll have to find the original videos and then you'll probably find yourself patiently trying to explain why they were funny. (via Metafilter)

item.title: Kiah Stokes Is The Unlikely Star Of These Grueling WNBA Finals
item.author: Patrick Redford
item.content:encoded: Moments after the Golden State Valkyries wrapped up a dominant, ugly, 64-55 Game 5 win, the home PA announcer pulled in Valkyries center Kiah Stokes for an on-court interview. The crowd roared its approval with such deafening force that Stokes was completely drowned out. I wish I could tell you a single thing she said, though the crowd's "MVP!" chant was clear.The idea of a player who's averaging 4.3 points per game in the playoffs winning Finals MVP may seem a little ridiculous on its face, but these are no typical WNBA Finals, and Stokes is no typical defense-first center. These are the Finals of anti-basketball, the flow of the game only rarely doing anything besides oozing or sludging along as each team's excellent defense neutralizes their relatively inept counterparts. Stokes is more responsible for this than anyone else in these Finals, both for the way she's made the paint a zone of impossibility for the Dream, but also for her own peculiar offensive contributions. The box score captures some of what makes Stokes so special, though most of her impact eludes quantification. If you can see it, it's in the size of her shadow, an Angel Reese 2-for-8 night here, nine steals for Stokes's teammates there. Watch these Finals closely, and you'll see Stokes at the center of everything. https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=GEa8iMn-W4o

item.title: Does Your Dog Byte?
item.author: Dave Pell
item.source: NextDraft: The Day's Most Fascinating News
item.content:encoded: In a classic scene from the 1976 film The Pink Panther Strikes Again, Inspector Clouseau asks a hotel clerk, “Does your dog bite?” The clerk says no. When Clouseau reaches down to pet the dog, he is viciously bitten. So he says, “I thought you said your dog did not bite?” The hotel clerk explains, “That is not my dog.” One assumes that misunderstandings like this will be avoided on the streets of San Francisco where an industrious few are being offered twenty bucks an hour to walk robot-dogs. It somehow makes sense that we’re training robotic dogs. With all the sycophancy from Claude and ChatGPT, AI has already taken over the title of Man’s Best Friend. “On the positive side, there was no need to clean up after the robot, or to pretend you did not see the deposit it left behind on someone’s yard. On the negative side, the robots could prove as stubborn as their living counterparts. Just as a normal dog might suddenly plop down and refuse to budge in the middle of a busy street, the robot dogs, too, might give up mid-walk — because their equipment overheated. Robot dog walkers would then need to carry the mechanical quadrupeds back to the start-up’s office.” Kashmir Hill in the (Gift Article): Wanted: Robot-Dog Walkers. “Dimensional is building an open-source operating system for robots, said its founder, Stash Pomichter. Mr. Pomichter, who is 26, wants to embed A.I. agents in robots so that consumers can command them to do work in the real world.” Work? That’s definitely not my dog.+ : ICE plan to buy robot dogs spurs protest. “Hundreds of employees at the US robotics firm Boston Dynamics signed a petition calling for executives to halt a sale of the company’s robot dogs to US Immigration and Customs Enforcement—but executives stood by the deal, while saying the robots would not be weaponized.” Even Inspector Clouseau wouldn’t buy that…The economic divide is the issue that underpins many other problems in America. That said, I’m not sure a one-time, one-state wealth tax is a reasonable solution to the problem, but it’s worth noting how billionaires are banding together to fight the California proposal. The deep pockets in play make one wonder how any proposals that aim to at least slightly level the playing field could get passed. “Every Tuesday for the last few months, two dozen of the world’s richest people or their advisers hop onto a conference call and plan for war. The war is against a proposed tax, but not just any tax. It is against a ‘wealth tax’ on California billionaires, one that Silicon Valley’s most affluent see as an existential threat that could usher in a new way of attacking them. So in confidential memos, WhatsApp and Signal chats and conference calls, they are banding together to battle back. The calls are organized by Building a Better California.” (Ironically, Building a Better California is a nonprofit.) (Gift Article): Inside the Billionaires’ War Against California’s Proposed Wealth Tax.+ “Since John D. Rockefeller handed out dimes, the world’s richest have given away their money in very different ways. Now they are bypassing charity—and writing a new social contract.” (Gift Article): Billionaires Stave off the Pitchforks With Payouts to One Kid at a Time. (The kids get a few bucks, and when the donations are made in stock, millions of them will have an interest in your company’s stock price performing well. Hand out dimes. Make quarters.)“A president who derides wind turbines as cancer-causing, stalls the nation’s first offshore wind permit and denies the urgency of climate change would surely become the industry’s greatest obstacle. Yet markets sometimes focus on the headline without understanding the underlying story. This may prove to be one of those moments … Public policy still matters. Elections matter. Regulations matter. Leadership matters. But there comes a point when economics exerts a force that politics can only slow, not reverse.” How Trump Unwittingly Boosted Green Energy.+ That doesn’t mean that years of terrible leadership haven’t cost America a hell of a lot when it comes to the green economy. (Gift Article): I went to Mexico to test-drive the cars Americans can’t buy. “Chinese branded vehicles have gone from less than 1 percent to 15 percent market share in five years, as well as about 90 percent of all EVs. That’s fast eroding America’s market in its backyard, as well as abroad, where the U.S. has seen its share fall or stagnate in Asia, Europe and Latin America. Even at home, the Big Three now command less than 40 percent of the auto market, down from 92 percent in 1965.” (It sure looks like Tony Manero’s hardware store boss in got it right when he explained, “You can’t f-ck the future. The future f-ucks you! It catches up with you and it f-cks you if you ain’t planned for it.”)Smoking is back. That’s definitely true in movies and TV series, where the cigarette has returned as the most omnipresent prop. It’s true in the pages of magazines. And it’s increasingly true when it comes to celebrity culture. The somewhat surprising return of cigarettes to pop culture is having a big impact on real life. And I’m not just blowing smoke. “Among 18 to 24-year-olds surveyed by Truth Initiative, a nonprofit public health organization dedicated to preventing youth and young adult nicotine addiction, 25% said ‘smoking makes people look cool’ in 2026, up from 17% in 2019. Nearly half — 47% — said ‘it is not a big deal if my friends smoke,’ compared with 38% seven years earlier. And 21% associated smoking with fitting in, up from 14% in 2017. The swing was even more pronounced among younger teens: In 2026, 21% of 15 to 17-year-olds agreed that smoking helps people fit in, up from 4% in 2017.” Is smoking cool again? New data suggests some young people are warming to the idea. “Most Americans can identify at least one value from a list of 12 that they believe is widely shared in the country. Only a quarter say none of the values are still shared. Yet, there is little consensus on which values are widely shared, or which the country needs more of. Even so, 79% of Americans say respecting different values matters more than sharing the same ones.” In U.S., Three-Quarters Identify Shared Values. (Hate is not our natural state. It has to be stirred by those who benefit from it.)+ “Here is another measure of Cubans’ anger at their government: During nine days of travel around the island, I did not meet a single person who blamed Donald Trump or the United States for their situation. I sometimes reminded them about the blockade Trump had started earlier this year, cutting Cubans off from the cheap oil that Venezuela had been supplying before the U.S. military captured Nicolás Maduro in January. Hadn’t things gotten worse since then? ‘I don’t see any change since January,’ a retired engineer named Guillermo Almeida told me. ‘That oil from Venezuela wasn’t reaching the people anyway.'” Robert F. Worth in (Gift Article): The Collapse of Cuba. “I drove to the east with the photographer Moises Saman, an 18-hour journey that sometimes made us feel as if we were traveling back in time.”+ Unsurprisingly, Israel is seeing record turnout in what is expected to be a close election. Here’s the latest from the NYT and Times of Israel. In Israel, people vote for parties, not individual candidates, and, if none of the parties get a majority, they need to form coalitions to pick a leader. So this all could take a while.+ “It would almost be funny if it weren’t such an appalling abuse of the Department of Justice – one that we cannot become numb to. Nothing’s changed with me; I’m still innocent, I’m still not afraid of these people — and I still believe in an independent federal judiciary.” Trump is going after James Comey … again.+ “The man who has helped produce the Super Bowl halftime show is stepping into the spotlight: Jay-Z will headline the show himself.” (This is like when Dick Cheney chose himself to be W’s running mate, but with a much higher likelihood of Beyonce being involved.)+ “From the Department of ‘We sent a man to the moon but we can’t [do some simple thing]’ comes word that Cheerios is boldly going where no cereal has before: a resealable Ziploc bag.”“They called the police on a 3-year-old because he had the ball for too long.” Parents say police were called because their 3-year-old was ‘too good’ at soccer. (The kid is pretty damn good. And yes, this happened in Florida.)

item.title: Thumb on the Scales

item.content:encoded: The U.S. Department of Justice has notified several Georgia counties it intends to station monitors there on Election Day.Bibb, Cobb, Chatham, DeKalb, Fulton and Gwinnett counties have received notifications from the Justice Department. Each of those counties has produced solid wins for Democrats in recent elections.The Justice Department routinely sends election monitors to polling locations to ensure compliance with laws and that voters’ rights are protected. But given the Trump administration’s actions to assert more federal control over elections and investigate the president’s 2020 election grievances, the notices have raised concerns among Democrats and some election officials about what the monitors might try to do in November.

item.title: Troma Tuesday: Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters
item.author: Schill
item.content:encoded: There are movies that are difficult to explain.Then there are movies like Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters, where explaining the plot might actually make the movie sound less believable than simply watching it.Released in 1982, this bizarre Troma release is an American reworking of the Indonesian action film . Directed by Jopi Burnama with Charles Kaufman involved in the Troma version, the movie takes Indonesian martial-arts and wrestling footage, strips away the original soundtrack and adds a completely new English-language comedic dub. The result is part action movie, part exploitation film and part drunken midnight-movie commentary track.In other words, exactly the sort of thing Troma would distribute.The basic story actually sounds reasonably serious.Bambi, played by Indonesian action star Eva Arnaz, is a former judo champion who wants to get away from the fighting business. Unfortunately, her family needs money. Her younger brother requires an expensive operation, leaving Bambi with very few options. She eventually gets involved with a female wrestling operation, which pulls her into a world involving shady characters, violence and criminal activity.That sounds like the setup for a gritty Indonesian martial-arts drama.And then Troma got hold of it.The American version is essentially a giant joke built around footage that was originally intended to be taken much more seriously. The dialogue was redubbed, the tone was transformed and the movie was presented as a bizarre comedy. The American version runs roughly 74 minutes, considerably shorter than the original Indonesian version, which has also been released under titles including .This is where Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters becomes fascinating.The actual action footage is frequently pretty impressive.Eva Arnaz was a genuine Indonesian action star, and the original production gives her plenty to do. There are martial-arts sequences, wrestling matches, fights and criminal-syndicate shenanigans. The movie comes from an era of Indonesian exploitation cinema when filmmakers were producing wildly energetic genre movies with a mixture of martial arts, melodrama, horror and adventure.Troma looks at all of that and essentially says:“Yeah, but what if everyone sounded completely ridiculous?”The redubbing is the star of the American version.Instead of trying to create a convincing English-language adaptation, the new dialogue goes straight for absurdity. Characters suddenly sound like they’re participating in an entirely different movie. Serious scenes become jokes. Dramatic confrontations become opportunities for ridiculous dialogue.It’s basically after somebody replaced Woody Allen with the Troma crew.And the weirdness doesn’t stop there.One of the movie’s most famously ridiculous plot points involves Bambi’s brother and an extraordinarily strange medical condition that supposedly requires an operation. The premise is so completely bonkers that attempting to discuss it seriously feels like a waste of everyone’s time.Then there is Barry Prima, another major Indonesian action star, playing Barney. In a normal version of the movie, his character is a martial-arts figure involved in Bambi’s increasingly complicated situation. In the Troma version, he becomes part of the lunacy, with the dubbing turning him into one of the movie’s many sources of comic absurdity.What makes the whole thing work is the contrast.You have serious-looking action footage.You have beautiful Indonesian locations.You have actors who clearly know how to perform martial arts.You have dramatic music and editing from the original production.And over the top of all of it, you have dialogue that sounds like it was written by people who had absolutely no intention of respecting the source material.The movie is also very much a product of Troma’s early-’80s philosophy. Troma didn’t necessarily need every film it handled to be technically polished. It needed personality.And Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters has personality coming out of every available hole.The biggest problem is that the joke can become repetitive. Once you understand what Troma has done, the basic formula doesn’t change much. Serious scene appears. Ridiculous dialogue arrives. Fight happens. More ridiculous dialogue follows.Eventually, you know exactly what the movie is going to do.But then something completely insane happens anyway.That unpredictability keeps it alive.The movie also benefits from being short. At around 74 minutes in its American re-edited form, it doesn’t have much time to become boring.Because this is not a movie you watch for character development.You’re not emotionally invested in Bambi’s journey because you’ve spent three hours getting to know her.You’re here for the fights.You’re here for the dubbing.You’re here for the sheer audacity of taking a relatively straightforward Indonesian action film and transforming it into something that feels like an entirely different genre.The film is also an interesting reminder of how strange the international exploitation business could be before streaming made practically every movie in the world accessible from a laptop.Troma’s version effectively created a new movie out of an existing one. The original was an Indonesian action drama, while Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters became an American cult comedy through editing and dubbing.Today, that concept might sound familiar, but in the context of Troma’s catalog it fits perfectly.It’s a movie that exists because somebody looked at perfectly usable martial-arts footage and thought it would be much funnier if everyone suddenly started saying ridiculous things.The strangest thing about Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters is that underneath all the Troma nonsense, there’s a legitimate action movie struggling to escape.Eva Arnaz is charismatic.The fight scenes have genuine energy.The Indonesian setting gives the movie a visual identity that most low-budget American exploitation movies simply couldn’t duplicate.Then the dubbing comes crashing through the door and starts throwing pies at everything.That’s the entire experience.If you’re expecting a serious martial-arts movie, you’ll probably be confused.If you’re expecting a conventional comedy, you’ll probably be confused.If you’re expecting Troma to take something completely straight-faced and turn it into a deranged midnight movie, you’re exactly where you need to be.Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters isn’t necessarily a great movie.But it is a .It’s bizarre, cheap, energetic, occasionally offensive, frequently hilarious and completely incapable of behaving like a normal film.And honestly, that’s why it remains memorable.The movie doesn’t simply break the fourth wall.It grabs the fourth wall, throws it into a wrestling ring and starts beating it with a folding chair.Ferocious Female Freedom Fighters is exactly the kind of cinematic lunacy that makes cult-movie hunting worthwhile. The original Indonesian action footage is entertaining on its own, but Troma’s completely ridiculous redubbing turns it into something much stranger.It’s not a movie you watch because you need a coherent story.It’s a movie you watch because you want to see how badly someone can derail a perfectly respectable martial-arts film.Just don’t expect the title to be the strangest thing about it.

item.title: GPT-6.1 Terra
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: It's always interesting to note which aspects of a new model are emphasized in the release announcement.In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, OpenAI went with visual reasoning and computer use:We’re introducing , a fast, efficient model that combines detailed visual reasoning and precise computer use alongside clearer, more natural writing. A significant step up from GPT‑5.6 Terra, it excels at the communication and computer-based tasks that fill the workday, from drafting proposals and interpreting technical drawings to filling out forms and editing videos.Terra sits in the same position as Sonnet in the Anthropic model collection - not the cheapest or the most expensive, making it harder to decide when to use it.Computer use is a good example of a task that benefits from a less expensive model, since you might put it to work on automated, repetitive tasks.OpenAI's Ted Sanders provided some useful advice in a comment on Hacker News:In the case of GPT-6.1 Terra, I'd say Terra is probably better than Astra and Sol at technical communication, similar on vision and computer use (but much faster!), and a bit worse on most other things. For API developers, it's a nice midrange option if you want something cheaper than Sol but a lot smarter than Luna (especially for vision / computer use / communication). For subscribers, it's not a bombshell release - if you're hitting usage limits, maybe it helps you go a bit further, and if you want clearer communication or faster computer use, it can be a nice option to select.Here's a new comparison grid showing pelicans for every reasoning level of OpenAI's current frontier lineup: GPT-6 Astra, GPT-6.1 Sol, GPT-6.1 Terra, and GPT-6 Luna.GPT-6.1 Terra is priced at $1/million input tokens and $5/million output - almost half the price of GPT-5.6 Terra and GPT-6.1 Sol, and around 10x the price of GPT-6 Luna.

item.title: Fast Times in East Pennsboro Township — The Scott Perry Boogie Nights Story
item.author: Josh Marshall
item.source: Josh Marshall – TPM – Talking Points Memo
item.content:encoded: Every campaign season, especially ones as intense as this one, will churn up stories that aren’t so much about lying or scandal or low-rent tactics as they are simply some mix of desperate, weird and hilarious. The one I’m about to share manages to be all of those but mainly just hilarious and weird. Let’s go to Pennsylvania’s 10th congressional district, where longtime Freedom Caucuser and election denier Rep. Scott Perry (R) appears to be in the race of his life. Members of the Freedom Caucus, as you’d expect, are usually from very, very red districts where you can indulge the Freedom Caucus lifestyle with few electoral repercussions. But that’s never really been the case with Perry. Cook Report says it’s an R+3 district and Perry beat Janelle Stelson, a former local news broadcaster, by only 5,000 votes in 2024, hardly a strong Democratic year.Stelson is challenging Perry again this year and now most polls show him running behind.So he has a new campaign attack: Stelson walks around naked!

item.title: WNBA Moves Potential Title-Clinching Finals Game To Lunchtime
item.author: Maitreyi Anantharaman
item.content:encoded: The WNBA was faced with the following issue: After the first four games of the WNBA Finals, played at the raucous 18,064-seat Chase Center in San Francisco and then at equally raucous 17,044-seat State Farm Arena in Atlanta, the Golden State Valkyries and the Atlanta Dream are tied at two games apiece. The teams will play a Game 5 in San Francisco on Monday night, and a now-necessary Game 6 on Thursday in Atlanta, where the Dream’s primary venue, Gateway Center Arena, seats just 3,500. You'll recall that this was the exact issue the league and the Dream had to scramble to resolve before the Finals started. Games 3 and 4 were originally scheduled for nights when State Farm Arena was already booked for a Sombr concert and the Atlanta Hawks' home opener. The WNBA ultimately changed the Finals schedule to ensure that the Dream could host Games 3 and 4 in the larger venue. They've now hosted all their home games there this postseason.But at the time, the Dream and WNBA didn't settle on a plan for what would happen if the series went six games. The Hawks, the building's primary tenant, are again scheduled to host a game against the Cleveland Cavaliers, the same night as Game 6 on Thursday. With only one travel day scheduled between Game 6 and Saturday's Game 7, there wasn't as much room to futz around with the schedule this time. After the Valkyries guaranteed a sixth game with Saturday's win, ESPN's Alexa Philippou and Ramona Shelburne reported that the league was considering a number of solutions, none of them ideal. One, in fact, seemed totally ridiculous: playing Game 6 as a Thursday matinee.

item.title: Proton To ‘Re-Interview’ Staff About AI To See Who Gets To Keep Their Job
item.author: Joseph Cox
item.content:encoded: Proton, the company behind ProtonMail and other privacy-focused products, told staff on Monday it would be ‘re-interviewing’ staff across the company about how they use AI in their jobs, with the implication that the interviews may decide whether staffers have “continued employment,” according to an internal Proton email obtained by 404 Media.“These re-interviews are consequential,” a part of the email reads. “Interviewers will document their assessments, which will inform the broader review of our organization and talent. That review may lead to changes in roles, responsibilities, and continued employment. Individual outcomes will be communicated directly once decisions are finalized.”Proton’s CEO Andy Yen has steadily pushed the company towards more AI use, including launching AI centered products like Lumo, a privacy-focused chatbot. The leaked email says Yen “interviewed more than 40 senior leaders across Engineering and Product to begin this process.” Now, those interviews are extending across the company.“We need people who can translate AI’s capabilities into better products, stronger execution, and new ways of working — and who approach this change with curiosity, judgment, and urgency,” the email reads.The email says that not everyone in the company will be re-interviewed, and “any decisions affecting your employment will be communicated separately.” The interviewer will be outside the staff member’s team and reporting line; instead, people may be interviewed by someone from “a pool of leaders who demonstrate strong AI capability and have aligned on the assessment criteria.”“We recognize that this process creates uncertainty. We will be clear about what has been decided and what remains open, and communicate individual outcomes as soon as we can,” the email adds. It says the re-interviews will take place between November 4 and 11.Proton did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

item.title: Positive alerts in Prometheus
item.author: Alex Chan
item.content:encoded: At work, we use Prometheus to monitor our services. Every few seconds, Prometheus scrapes a endpoint and records the data in a time series database. The metrics are then used to trigger alerts when services aren’t behaving correctly.Recently we had a flapping alert where an overloaded service was intermittently failing. We wanted to silence/adjust the alert until we could fix the service, to avoid alert fatigue, but it would be easy to forget to revert the adjustment once the service was fixed.We solved this using a “positive alert” that would tell us when the service was consistently passing the original alert – that is, when it was no longer flapping.Let’s walk through an example. One of our alerts checks that Prometheus can successfully scrape our services, which you can check with the automatically generated time series. A successful scrape gets a , a failed scrape gets a .Here’s an alert that warns if more than 5% of scrapes fail within a half hour window:groups name rules alert expr for labels severity annotations summaryOne of our services was struggling to serve the endpoint that Prometheus scrapes. When the service had a lot of work in its queue, the worker thread would starve the web server and the metrics request would fail. The scrape rate would dip below 95%, the alert would fire, then the service would empty its queue and the rate would recover, the alert would clear, and so we went round and round. Dozens of notifications which were nothing but noise.We use Alertmanager Silences when we want to pause an alert for a short period, but it wasn’t clear if or when we’d be able to fix this service. If the silence expired before the problem was fixed, the noise would return. If the problem was fixed before the silence expired, we could unknowingly regress the fix.Instead, we modified the alert to exclude the overloaded service, then added a “positive alert” to tell us if the service had more than 95% uptime for a fortnight:groups name rules alert expr for labels severity annotations summary alert expr for labels severity annotations summaryThis worked exactly as intended. A few weeks ago, one of my colleagues made changes to improve the overloaded service, and Prometheus was able to crawl it consistently. The alert fired at the weekend as it ticked over a fortnight of continuous uptime, and we removed the exception.

item.title: NASA’s Perseverance Sets Off-World Record for Total Distance Driven
item.author: Jason Kottke
item.content:encoded: On Oct. 11, the rover’s odometer reached 28.10 miles (45.22 kilometers), eclipsing the record of 28.06 miles (45.16 kilometers) set by NASA’s Opportunity rover, which explored Mars from 2004 to 2018. Perseverance reached the mark on the 2,006th Martian day, or sol, of its mission, covering in five and a half years a distance that took Opportunity almost 15.For a vehicle whose top speed is 0.1 mph and which stops all the time to do science, 28 miles is quite a distance. The route video is fun to watch…it resembles a dog’s path, sniffing out its favorite spots and doubling back along familiar routes.BTW, the Guinness World Record for the number of miles driven by one vehicle on Earth is 3,039,122 miles. (And the guy kept driving it after the record was recorded…he reached 3,260,257 miles before he died.)

item.title: MAGA attacks on women voters are no joke
item.content:encoded: If the polls are correct, Republicans are set for a shellacking in the Nov. 3 midterms, losing the House and quite possibly the Senate, and likely some prominent governorships across the country. If that happens, there’s a good chance that online chatter about repealing the 19th Amendment will heat up once again.For a decade now, MAGA social media users have been aggrieved at the way women vote for Democrats at higher rates then men, such as in 2024, when 53% of women voted for Kamala Harris over Donald Trump, who received 55% of the male vote. Their solution to this imbalance began in 2016 as a trolling hashtag on what was then called Twitter: #RepealThe19th, a reference to the constitutional amendment, ratified in 1920, that extended suffrage to all women in theory, but mostly white women in practice. The hashtag has faded since then, but not because of a lack of interest. The idea has morphed from a joke into a serious proposal that is making its way from fringe Christian right circles into the mainstream of the Republican Party.Douglas Wilson, a prominent Christian nationalist who lead the church Pete Hegseth belongs to, has grown increasingly loud in his calls to replace individual voting with “household voting,” where only heads of households, who are presumably male, would be able to vote. The defense secretary has praised Wilson for a CNN interview he gave in which he outlined his vision of a Christian theocracy that disenfranchises women. Ending women’s suffrage is a hot topic among the right’s youngest leaders. Earlier this year, “Conversation over whether women should vote used to be limited to some of the most extreme and patriarchal churches,” said Sarah Stankorb, a journalist, expert in women and religion, and author of “Damned If She Does: Why Women Quit Church and What It Means for the Future of Religion.” She told Salon that it’s “no coincidence” that ideas once on the fringes of the Christian right “keep popping up in public discourse.”Stankorb noted that Christian nationalists are taking “partisan polarization” to a place where “denying the basic rights of half the population not only comes off as a debatable point, but one with theological backing.” “All at once, patriarchal men share think-pieces on walking back the 19th, while perched casually in leather chairs, normalizing the conversation as if it’s simply academic, reasonable even,” she said. Stankorb is worried that the constant social media repetition means the shock has “dulled over time,” putting the once unthinkable “in the realm of ‘normal.'”To be certain, it’s extremely unlikely that Christian nationalists will be able to repeal the 19th Amendment, which would require passing and ratifying a new amendment. There is precedent for this; after the 18th Amendment, which banned the sale of alcohol, was ratified, it took another amendment, the 21st, to overturn Prohibition. The process would require a joint resolution approved by two-thirds of the House and Senate or a constitutional convention, followed by approval of three-fourths, or 38 out of 50, statesAs extreme as the GOP has gotten, it’s hard to imagine that the party — which has 11 sitting female Senators — would go that far, or be able to win big enough majorities in Congress, if they even considered it. After all, it took a century of feminist organizing to get male leaders to even let women vote, and it would be a lot harder to take the right away since over half the electorate is female. The larger goal here is to normalize the idea that women’s citizenship isn’t legitimate and to instill the idea that women should feel lucky to be “allowed” even the few rights they have.In all likelihood, most of the MAGA pundits and pastors who are pushing to end women’s suffrage know full well it will never happen. But their musings shouldn’t be dismissed as nothing more than attention-seeking behavior. The larger goal here is to normalize the idea that women’s citizenship isn’t legitimate and to instill the idea that women should feel lucky to be “allowed” even the few rights they have. In fact, this notion is similar to the way that leaders like Vice President JD Vance insist people of color should be “grateful” for having rights at all, words which carry the implication that the way to prove their gratitude is by not demanding full equality. Wilson made the underlying threat explicit in April. “Women have to appeal to men for the rights,” he told Konstantin Kisin, a right-wing British political commentator. “Anytime men want to take rights away from women, they can, like that. And there’s not a damn thing women can do about it.” Wilson continued to argue that there will no end to male dominance, because if women push their luck too far, it will be the end of male “benevolence” in letting women have any rights at all. His diatribe shows the goal of the anti-suffrage argument: to scare women off seeking full equality, or even trying to claw back rights they do have.While the 19th Amendment is unlikely to be repealed, it’s important to note that other rights that were long assumed to be safe have been stripped from women in the MAGA era. The right to abortion, which was for decades widely assumed to be untouchable, was overturned by a far-right Supreme Court in 2022. Because of women’s outrage — and suffrage — many red states restored abortion rights through ballot measures, which angered the right and amplified calls to take away women’s votes.The assumption that the justice system will protect women and children from sexual violence has also been under assault in recent years with actions that range from the Trump administration blocking the release of the Epstein files to the attacks on the Cornell student whose only “crime” was reporting an alleged gang rape. Then there is the recent ad run by Ohio’s Republican gubernatorial candidate Vivek Ramaswamy, which features the estranged mother of Dr. Amy Acton, his Democratic opponent. In 1978, after Acton reported that she had been raped by her stepfather, her mother sided with her husband, and the pair fled the state following his arrest and before he could stand trial.All these incursions on women’s rights are easier to sell to a public that has normalized the idea that women aren’t full citizens — that their ability to vote is a privilege that can be snatched away, and suffrage is only a right for men. The voting rights issue is used as a rhetorical cudgel against women, designed to delegitimize their opinions by suggesting they aren’t even real citizens. It’s about scaring women into thinking that if they “abuse” their vote by demanding full equality, they will be left with no rights at all.

item.title: LIV Golf Given A Few More Days To Climb Out Of The Grave
item.author: Chris Thompson
item.content:encoded: It is getting harder to find header photos for these LIV Golf updates. The LIV Golf 2026 season wrapped, prematurely, back in August, when the broke promotion hastily jammed its individual and team championships into one final, somewhat quieter tournament in Indianapolis, then folded up the tents and laid off basically everyone who is not a lawyer or CEO Scott O'Neil. Everything that's happened since then has taken place in conference rooms and bankruptcy courts. There are only so many interesting images featuring that damn logo up there, and we have already used or considered all of them. Finding another photo is stressful and tedious.It's delightful to think that soon there might be a final LIV Golf blog. O'Neil has yet to formally secure investment for what he has dubbed LIV 2.0. He has an investor, an "alternative investment management" firm called BC Partners, but there are still balls in the air and nothing is final. BC Partners set a deadline of Oct. 25 for the promotion to secure commitments from enough players for the reshaped tour to remain viable. If you check your calendar this morning, you will note that Oct. 25 was yesterday. The reported Sunday that "around 15 players have expressed interest" in remaining with LIV Golf, which is short of the "30 to 40 players" sought by BC Partners.This is one of those glass-half-empty situations: You will note that 15 is a lot less than 40, and is thus not ideal, and is in fact less than half of ideal. But 15 is also not nothing, and not nothing was evidently enough for O'Neil and BC Partners to extend the deadline to the end of this week. The calls the tentative commitments of these players "enough interest for the startup league to seek a final deal in the coming days."

item.title: webframe: evaluated as a scraper and a sandbox
item.author: Simon Willison
item.content:encoded: webframe is a neat little project from Jeff Lindsay which lets you "run a web page like a program" - you point it at a URL or file and it executes it in a hidden headless web view and outputs to standard output and any exceptions to standard error.It's written in Go on top of the glaze library, which provides access to a system browser ("WKWebView on macOS, WebKitGTK on Linux, WebView2 on Windows") so it doesn't need to bundle its own browser engine.It reminds me of my own shot-scraper javascript tool, albeit in a much smaller package that doesn't depend on Playwright.Explore https://github.com/tractordev/webframe try running it and put it though its paces, build a few exploratory prototypes, then evaluate it as a potential sandboxing tool and as a tool for scraping web pages using the same patterns encouraged by the "shot-scraper JavaScript" command (see simonw/shot-scraper on GitHub, docs directory)
